note: Source-evidenced classification of the Gate 0B.12 tranche. Ownership is accountability, not authorization: a classified operation names the engineering capability responsible for it, and every gap between that operation and a kernel decision is a recorded defect with one responsible capability. Every material claim of a record cites provenance: the exact method handler, an import it uses, a service it reaches or a schema it resolves. A missing institutional mandate does not prevent an engineering owner and no capability was invented to reduce SCOPE_UNDECIDED. No institutional decision recorded here is adopted, and none justifies access. The four carbon operations are not part of this tranche; they are held in the decision-bound scope exception register.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which platform staff may read across organizations or operate shared platform services, under what mandate, scope, expiry and audit?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The source uses a platform_lead role title and an isPlatformAdminUser identity check. Neither is an issued, scoped, expiring mandate. No adopted decision in the repository names a platform-staff mandate model.

institutionalDecisions.question: Does the approved per-organization representation protocol, or the kernel issuance model, decide who holds representation authority over a case?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The case-assignment engine refuses to assign without an approved protocol. The kernel also issues mandates and assignments. The source does not say which governs when they differ.

institutionalDecisions.question: Who may mark a knowledge-base row or collective agreement is_public, and what review precedes publication beyond the organization?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: AI search and summarize return another organization's row when is_public is true. Agreement creation sets isPublic false and says publication is not decided at creation. No source says who sets the flag.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which roles may read the organization audit history, and which fields must be withheld from each?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The activity feed and AI usage routes return audit-derived rows at member and administrator role floors. No adopted decision names the readers.

institutionalDecisions.question: Is observability alerting an organization-administration, platform-operations or security-monitoring obligation, and who may read its alerts?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The realtime alerts route returns an organization's alert rows at the member role floor under the grievance case suite entitlement. No capability or persona source names observability alerting.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which organization office may read the commercial terms of, pause, resume or cancel the organization platform subscription, and which of those acts belong to the platform operator?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: Subscription reads sit at the member floor, pause and resume at the steward floor, and metadata update and cancel at the secretary_treasurer role title, a union finance role. The Financial Officer disposition labels the platform billing service as not union finance. No adopted decision names the contract-authority office.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which capability and which organization office own newsletter campaigns, recipients and delivery status, and is campaign delivery status a billing or a communications obligation?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The batch-status route lives under billing and is gated by a billing entitlement but reads newsletter_campaigns and newsletter_recipients. No capability, persona source or register entry names campaigns or newsletter delivery.

institutionalDecisions.question: Does the platform operator or an organization own carbon accounting, and which measured data source, if any, may back an emissions figure or a neutrality claim?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The carbon routes return emissions figures written as literals in the handler, take the organization from the query string and are called by no product source; no table, service, persona source or capability record names carbon accounting.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which offices may read the training registrations, completions, certifications and session details (meeting access codes, budgets, accommodation) of other members of an organization, and may a member see a session they are not registered for?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The training routes are the generic CRUD factory: registrations, completions and certifications are held to the caller own member id at every role, so no office reads another member record, while sessions are readable in full by any member of the organization. No source names an education officer, instructor or steward mandate for training records.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which office may mark a registration completed, issue a certificate or certification number, verify a certification and revoke it, and what evidence of completion must exist first?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: Any steward writes completed, passed, certificateIssued, certificateNumber and verified through the generic create route, and a member who registers can supply the same fields in the body; member_certifications.verified defaults to true. No source names an issuing or verifying authority.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which office may open an employer request for workers and assign members to it, and which rules (seniority, rotation, availability, skills) bind the assignment?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: A steward opens a request and an officer assigns any member ids from the body; the dispatch rules table has no write route and the ranking function is called by no route. No adopted decision names the dispatch office or the rule order.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which office may state that a deadline, quorum or certification threshold is met, and from which governed source of statutory parameters?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The validate route returns compliant and violation verdicts from numbers in the request body against thresholds written as literals in the handler; no adopted decision names the office or the parameter source.

institutionalDecisions.question: Does the union hold voter support levels, canvassing notes and elected-official contact records, who may read them, and under which privacy and political-finance rules?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: Political campaign, canvassing and official tables exist only in the financial-service schema and the interfaces expect voter support fields; the application routes are the generic factory over donation campaigns. No adopted decision names the holder or the readers.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which office owns the organization business-continuity, archive and succession (inheritance) records, what do those records contain, who may read them and how long must they be kept?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The continuity archives and docs paths are aliases of the document repository route, and the continuity inheritance path is the generic CRUD factory over the pending_profiles table, which holds pre-signup membership payment data and is refused by the CRUD governance table. No schema table, service, screen or capability-registry entry names a continuity plan, archive or succession record, so no source states what the obligation is or who holds it.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which offices may read the full text, attached documents and transcripts, event notes and AI summary of an exit interview at each sensitivity level, is the consent of the retiring member a precondition of publication, of reading and of any model or search use, who may record that consent or its withdrawal on the retiree behalf, and who owns the knowledge archive that the published copy lives in?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The code carries two incompatible answers. SENSITIVITY_MIN_ROLE names a minimum role per level (member, steward, officer, admin) and the search, summary and AI routes apply it, while the interview list, the interview item, the document list and the knowledge-base copy made at publication are readable by any member of the organization at every level. Consent defaults to false, gates only the embedding step, and is recorded by an administrator, not by the retiree. No source names an archive owner, a records officer or a legal-review step for legal_sensitive interviews.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which offices may read analytics, topic maps, single-source flags and event notes derived from exit interviews classified privileged, legal_sensitive or executive_confidential, and must such interviews be excluded from, or redacted in, the aggregates that a steward or officer reads?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The consent policy table assigns a minimum role to each sensitivity level and the AI search and summary routes apply it, while the steward and officer analytics routes aggregate every published interview, and the governance timeline every interview of the window, without reading sensitivityLevel. No adopted decision names the office or the aggregation rule.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which offices may read topic graphs, expertise and dependency analyses, resilience indexes and succession reports computed from exit interviews, and does a derived figure or label inherit the reader floor of the most sensitive interview it was computed from?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: Reading an interview is gated by its sensitivity level (public_internal member, restricted steward, privileged officer, legal_sensitive and executive_confidential admin), but the derived routes read every published interview whatever its level: the topic graph and the propagation map answer a steward, the resilience index, roadmap, succession report and the two aggregators answer an officer. No source states whether a topic label, role or count computed from an admin-only interview may be shown below admin.

institutionalDecisions.question: May exit-interview content (titles, topics, risk flags, roles and years of service) be sent to a model provider for an organization-wide analysis, which sensitivity levels are excluded, and does retiree consent or an office approval have to exist first?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: Consent is recorded per interview and consent-controls applies it only to semantic indexing and to publishing a legal_sensitive interview; the interview summarize route applies the sensitivity floor before it calls a model, and the succession report applies neither the sensitivity floor nor consent before it sends every published interview to the model. No source names who decides what may leave the organization.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which office of the union holds equity self-identification answers, who may read an individual answer and who only aggregates, what minimum group size suppresses a published count, how long an answer is kept and how Indigenous data governance (ownership, control, access, possession) is honoured?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The self-identification form text promises encryption, aggregate-only reporting with a ten-member minimum, withdrawal and deletion at any time, seven-year retention and Indigenous data governance, but no adopted decision, schema table, service or route names the data steward, the readers, the minimum cell size or the retention rule. The only equity table, equity_snapshots, is declared in the financial-service schema, is revoked from the application runtime and system roles, and stores executive-board and steward counts by group and average pay by gender with no suppression rule.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which office may register, change and remove an external SAML or OIDC identity provider for an organization, how is the organization shown to own the identity domain the provider asserts, and which provider groups may confer which tenant roles?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The register route lets any administrator of the organization insert a provider with an unverified issuer or entity id, defaults autoProvision and enabled to true and limits the role mapping to the four tenant-assignable roles; no source names an identity-federation office, a domain ownership proof or a review by platform staff, and no sign-in path reads the table.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which offices of the union may read the injured-person, injury, treatment, witness, investigation and compensation-claim fields of a workplace incident, the reporter and assignee fields of a hazard report and the issuance records of PPE, and does any member below the health and safety representative floor read an incident or a hazard report by id?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The incident and hazard collection routes require health_safety_rep while the by-id routes of the same tables require member, no source names the offices that may read an incident row, the table carries injured person name, treatment, witness statements and WSIB claim fields, and the application records no audit of any read.

institutionalDecisions.question: Does the union offer anonymous reporting of incidents and hazards, which offices may learn the identity of an anonymous reporter, and where is that identity kept (the record, the audit trail or neither)?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The incident and hazard report forms offer a Report anonymously option and the create hooks blank the reporter name and contact, but the factory stamps createdBy with the session user and the audit record names the user; no source states a policy on who may learn an anonymous reporter identity.

institutionalDecisions.question: How long may a pseudonymous ICRA assessment, its free-text notes, its consent record and its organization context be kept, who may erase them, and must a respondent be able to withdraw an assessment that they started?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The ICRA routes create assessments, answers with free-text notes and organization context rows and offer no delete or withdraw route; the capability expires after 30 days but the rows do not, and a source comment states the notes are not PII-safe by construction. No adopted decision names a retention period or an erasure office.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which office may approve or reject the narrative slot of an ICRA report before it is shown or sent, and how is that decision attributed to a person?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The review route accepts the shared cron secret and a reviewer role named in the request body; it names no person or office and the audit record, when written, names a constant system actor. No adopted decision names the reviewing office.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which office of an organization may claim a purchased ICRA assessment into the tenant, must that office be the purchaser, and what does each paid report tier deliver once claimed?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The claim route binds the assessment to the organization of any signed-in user who presents a claim token and checks no role; no code issues an ICRA claim token, and the tier copy promises an executive PDF that the report route does not release. No adopted decision names the claiming office or the tier deliverable.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which office of an organization may configure, activate and run an external provider integration, and who holds and rotates the credential material that the integration uses?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The framework routes allow any steward to configure, activate and synchronize an approved provider; credentials are a placeholder reference that nothing resolves, and the api-keys route is refused by governance. No adopted decision names the office or the credential custody.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which shop and which office decide that a reward redemption was ordered, fulfilled or refunded, and may a refund return the full credit amount or only the amount the shop refunded?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The webhook receiver trusts one global Shopify signing secret for every organization, applies any refund event as a full credit return and never reads the shop domain. No adopted decision names the shop, the organization binding or the refund rule.

institutionalDecisions.question: What may a federation see of its affiliates (member counts, per-capita remittances, meeting records, grievance benchmarks), who in the federation may see it, how is the parent and child relationship between a federation organization and an affiliate established and verified, and what minimum group size suppresses a published grievance statistic?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The federations table links one organization to one federation row (organization_id is unique) and carries aggregate counters, but no source states which organization is the parent of which, who verifies an affiliation, or what an affiliate agrees to disclose; the affiliates, dashboard, meetings and remittances paths and the grievance benchmark path read none of it, and the generic governance table leaves federations READ_ONLY and grievances OWN_ROWS_READ.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which files may an outside representative deposit on a grievance, through which intake that scans and sizes the file, and which office reviews a deposited file before it joins the case record and before any other party can see it?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The upload route accepts a storage path or URL inside the organization document prefix, derives the document grant from the matter grant, and refuses privilege labels, but no source names the office that approves what an outside party attaches, no route lets an outside party place a new file in storage, and the intake prefix that holds scanned uploads is excluded from this route.

institutionalDecisions.question: For which purposes may the union collect a member precise position, which office may read an individual position or a geofence entry, how is a consent bound to a purpose, an organization and a strike or event, and which office owns the retention and the erasure of the points a member produced without an active consent?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The consent row is keyed by the member user id alone and carries a free-text purpose and two flags (strike, events); the tracking route checks the flags for strike, picket and event points and nothing for meeting and organizing points; the geofence entry check stores a position without reading the consent; no route reads a stored position back and no source names an office that may; the retention handler states an hourly schedule that no scheduler entry in the repository invokes.

institutionalDecisions.question: May the union score individual members for churn risk from their case history, which office may read and act on a named member score, what must members be told, and how long may a score and its case-derived features be kept?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The churn-risk routes compute and store a per-member risk score and the case-derived features behind it and return the member name to any officer; no source names a purpose, a notice to members, a consent record, a retention period or the office that may act on a score, and no adopted decision does.

institutionalDecisions.question: What organization, member and case information may be sent to the external AI query service, who may ask it questions, and how is the answer it returns recorded and reviewed before it is relied on?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The natural-language query route sends a steward question, an unrestricted context value, the organization id and a shared bearer token to the service at AI_SERVICE_URL and returns whatever it answers; no source states a disclosure rule, a data class, a consent basis or a durable record of the questions, and no adopted decision does.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which offices may address an in-app or push notification to one member or to a group of members, in whose name does it appear to the recipient, may a member opt out of push and in-app notices by class, and which office owns the registry of member devices, including what happens to a device row when the device passes to another account or the member leaves the organization?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The notification create route lets any steward address any member of the organization with a caller-written title, message, link and payload and stores no sender; the generic push routes named subscribe and unsubscribe store a campaign row and never a subscription or an opt-out; two device tables (push_devices and mobile_devices) are written by two different routes and no route removes or deactivates either; no source names an office that may send, a class that a member may refuse, or a retention rule for device tokens, and the notification dispatcher is recorded as NOT_IMPLEMENTED pending a communications wave.

institutionalDecisions.question: What may an organization being onboarded see of other organizations (the federations and congresses it could join, the member counts of its peers, the clauses other organizations shared), and is any of it a declared public directory or does each item need the other organization to opt in?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: Federation discovery lists federations and congresses by name, province and member count to any officer, peer benchmarks compute averages over other organizations, and clause suggestions list shared clauses with source organization names; the handlers apply no organization predicate and rely on row-level-security policies that show a tenant only its own organization row. No adopted decision names what a prospective affiliate may see.

institutionalDecisions.question: What data and what institutional rule may an onboarding suggestion (a parent federation match, a peer benchmark, a national average, a recommended feature or integration, a suggested limit) rest on, and how must a suggestion that rests on a fallback or a literal be labelled?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: Match scores, relevance scores, feature lists, integration lists and suggested limits are literal weights and tables in lib/utils/smart-onboarding.ts, and the national averages fall back to hard-coded numbers when the CLC API is not configured; the responses carry no indication of the basis. No adopted decision names the source of any of them.

institutionalDecisions.question: Who may attest that an organization was created, a user was invited or a role was assigned during onboarding, must the attestation be produced by the action itself and not asserted by a caller, and who reads those events?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The onboarding events route lets any steward or higher record these milestones for free-text target user and role values without performing or verifying the action, and the transfers path is a wrapper over the same recorder. No adopted decision names the attesting office or the readers of the events.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which office of an organization may change its profile, contact details, settings, parent affiliation and lifecycle status (including archiving the organization), who verifies a change of parent, and which fields of an organization record (contacts, billing contact, settings, member counts, hierarchy position) may a signed-in user of another organization read?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The item route lets an organization administrator update the profile and settings of the organization and archive it, and refuses a change of parent or status unless the caller is a system administrator; the delete path archives with no such check, and the read path returns the whole record of any organization to any signed-in user. No source names the office that owns each field, who verifies a parent change, or what another organization may see; the 0108 policy comment states only that a tenant sees its own organization row.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which office of an organization may add a person to the organization and assign an organization role, may that office grant a role above its own, does the person have to accept before the membership is active, and which offices may read the full roster with contact details and membership numbers?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The roster route lets any member read every roster row with email, phone and membership number and lets a steward insert an active membership with any of five roles for any user id; the member directory route reads the same table through a case-policy based directory authority. No source states which office decides membership or grants an organization role, or how a person consents to being added.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which office of an organization decides what it shares with its federation, sector, province and the congress (clauses, precedents, anonymization, approval and approver role), may a federation change those settings for an affiliate, and which offices may read the log of other organizations that accessed the resources of the organization?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The sharing settings and cross-organization access log tables exist with defaults (sharing off, anonymization required, approval required, approver role admin), but no route reads or writes either table: the sharing-settings and access-logs routes are the generic factory over the organizations table, so no source shows who decides or who reads.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which offices of an organization may read an organizing campaign (target employer, workplace, strategy, employer vulnerabilities, organizing team, card and contact counts, election figures), may a member who is not on the organizing team or a steward read it, may a federation or a staff representative of another organization read it, and which fields of a campaign must stay restricted to the organizing team because disclosure to an employer exposes workers and organizers to retaliation?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The campaign routes let any member of the organization read every campaign row at the member floor and let a steward write it; the table has no confidentiality, team-membership or classification column that a route reads, and no source names the office that may read a campaign or the fields that are restricted.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which office of a union may prepare, approve and sign a certification application or other filing with a labour board or the NLRB, who attests the unit description, the showing of interest and the card count that the filing states, who transmits the filing and records the receipt, and may a draft form carry legal text that the software, rather than counsel, supplies?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The filing and form routes store a campaign row and transmit nothing; the filing wizard and the form generator expect a filing record and a PDF, and no source names the office that signs or files, the attestation of the card count, or the author of the legal content of a generated form.

institutionalDecisions.question: Who holds the signed authorization cards and the identities of the workers who signed or lead the organizing committee, who may count them and state a support percentage, which consent a worker gives before being contacted or enrolled in an outreach sequence by email or text, and how is the count that a filing relies on proved?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: No route or table in the application stores a card, a signer, a committee member, a workplace contact, a note or a sequence enrolment: the cards signed and contact counters are integers on the campaign row that a steward writes, and no source names the holder of the cards, the counting office, or the consent and unsubscribe rule for organizing outreach.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which offices may create, change and wind up a pension plan, enrol a member, record a contribution, issue a tax record and decide a benefit claim, which trustees or administrators hold that fiduciary authority, who may read plan funding figures, the enrolment list, retirement eligibility and the minutes of trustee meetings, and how is a member eligible to retire determined?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The pension routes now hold a member to their own claims, contributions and T4A records and limit administration to the secretary_treasurer role title (FINANCIAL_MEMBER_DATA_ROLES); the pension-authority source states that the trustee-administration authority is not yet implemented and the trustee create, update and delete routes answer 501. Plans, the enrolment list through retirement-eligibility, and trustee minutes remain readable by every member; the figures that stand for plan assets, funding and years of service, and the amount on a T4A record, are typed by the administrator; no route decides a benefit claim; no source names a trustee body or an eligibility rule.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which documents may the union publish to members through a member portal, which office may deposit or publish one, what file types, size limits, scanning and storage rules apply to a deposited file, which members or roles may read each document, and how long is it retained?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The two portal document routes are the generic CRUD factory over the cms_pages table: members list every page row of the organization, a steward inserts a row with any column including status, a file URL string and the role list, no file is received, stored or scanned by either route, and the allowed-roles and requires-auth columns are never applied; the file-receiving route that stores bytes, scans them and records an intake is /api/documents/upload, which these routes do not call.

institutionalDecisions.question: What proof binds an anonymous pilot applicant to an organization, which office may attest that binding, and what access, if any, may an applicant-typed organization claim give the stewards of that organization before the binding exists?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The public application form accepts responses.organizationId from an unauthenticated submitter and that claim decides which organization stewards pass the same-organization check on the application until a platform administrator binds an organization by id; the binding checks only that the organization exists and records the administrator, with no applicant proof. No adopted decision names the proof or the attesting office.

institutionalDecisions.question: Who may approve the commercial terms of a pilot, what acceptance by the applicant organization must exist before a contract, an invoice or a subscription is created for it, and what may the system record as signed or issued?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: One platform-tier administrator approves a typed member count and amount, a second administrator is needed only to differ from the one who bound the organization, and the commercial transition then inserts a contract, sets it active with a signature time, issues an invoice and activates a subscription without any acceptance by the organization. No adopted decision names the approving office or the acceptance step.

institutionalDecisions.question: Whose attestation and consent are required before a pilot testimonial, case study, time-saved figure or benchmark record is generated, stored or shown outside the pilot organization, and what basis may its figures rest on?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The reference profile builds a testimonial, hours saved, a case study and a benchmark record from response keys, a literal default quotation and score-derived figures and stores them as versioned snapshots; no consent or attestation step exists and no adopted decision names the approver or the basis.

institutionalDecisions.question: Who may read per-user pilot usage telemetry, champion lists, friction lists and conversion signals for an organization, may the platform read them across organizations, and what events may the signals rest on given that clients assert them?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The telemetry routes let an administrator name any organization id and return per-user activity, the events are written by any member with caller-asserted types and metadata, and the champion and conversion thresholds are computed from them. No adopted decision names the readers, the cross-organization mandate or the evidential basis of a signal.

institutionalDecisions.question: Who may seed demo data, purge it and bootstrap or reset a pilot organization, in which runtimes, and may fictional records live in the same tables as the real records of a pilot organization?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: An officer can seed fictional grievances and employers into their own organization and a platform-tier administrator can reset the organization at a fixture slug, in any runtime whose NZILA_MODE is pilot or demo, which includes the pilot deployment; the seeded rows carry no marker and are counted with real records. No adopted decision names the authority, the runtimes or the separation.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which memberships (active, suspended, removed), which organization states (active, inactive, suspended, archived) and which platform authority permit a user to select an organization as the working context of a session, and is each selection an audited event?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The legacy switch validates a membership row without reading its status or removal flag and lets an identifier on an environment list select any organization; the canonical switch limits the choice to active private memberships of active organizations and issues a new session bound to the choice; neither writes an audit record. No source names who may select an organization or whether a selection is recorded.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which platform office owns the monthly recurring revenue, churn and unit-economics figures of the platform subscriptions, which stored source (the subscription event log or the monthly snapshot table) is authoritative for each figure, and who may read them?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The mrr, churn and unit-economics routes return the same fixed object of three zeros and read no table; the subscription event, monthly recurring revenue snapshot and customer acquisition tables exist in the financial service schema and no route under app/api reads them. No source names the owner, the authoritative source or the readers.

institutionalDecisions.question: Does the union collect membership dues from members through the application by card, which processor account receives the funds and whose merchant account it is, how is a payment applied to the dues ledger and to a balance that is paid through other channels at the same time, what receipt or refund path applies, and what member data may be sent to the processor?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The member dues routes read a member dues ledger and can create a pending payment and a Stripe PaymentIntent for the whole outstanding balance, but the source states that member dues collection is not part of the initial launch and the initiation answers 501 unless UE_MEMBER_DUES_PAYMENTS=1; no source names the merchant account, the receipt or the refund path, and the intent metadata carries the organization id and the member user id.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which arbitration decisions and organization-contributed precedents may be read by members of which organizations, which offices may add a decision to the shared library or change what an organization contributed, how is a decision marked public or restricted and who reviews it before it is shared, and may an organization withdraw a contribution?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The library routes serve every arbitration_decisions row to any member at the member floor with the full text, grievor and embedding, and the comment on the create route says the library is shared across tenants and only a platform-elevated role may add to it; the contributed-precedent routes are the generic CRUD configuration over arbitration_precedents, a table keyed by source_organization_id that carries a sharing level, a shared-with list and an anonymization flag, none of which a read route applies; no source names the audience, the review step or the withdrawal rule.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which rewards are awarded automatically (work anniversaries, scheduled awards), under what rule and at what credit amount, how often may the scheduler run and what makes a run safe to repeat, do credits expire and who is told before they do, and which offices may export the awards, wallet ledger and budgets of an organization?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The rewards cron route runs anniversary awards, an expiration warning task and a scheduled-award task for every active organization on a shared secret; the anniversary task creates and issues an award for each member whose join date falls on today, with no record that the award was already made; the scheduled-award task is a placeholder that counts rules as processed; no writer of a credit expiry date was found, and the export route returns every award, ledger and budget row of the organization to any signed-in member; no source names the automation rules, the expiry policy or the export audience.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which offices may run a platform reconciliation, view its runs and exceptions and resolve or write off an exception, what makes a resolution or write-off valid (second approver, evidence, ledger entry), how is a run repeated or corrected, and is reconciliation of the organization platform billing a duty of the union or of the platform operator?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The reconciliation routes let an administrator run a reconciliation over platform invoices, payments and fee events for a period and resolve or write off the resulting exceptions on a live financial mandate check; a resolution is a status and a note only, no ledger or invoice row changes, the same administrator can run and resolve, and the bank and upload paths do not receive a bank statement; no source names who owns reconciliation, the write-off authority or the correction path.

institutionalDecisions.question: Who may read, edit, publish or share a saved report definition of an organization (its author only, offices the institution names, every member), what does the is_public flag mean, and may a definition that embeds filter values about members be visible to every member?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The report routes are generic CRUD over the reports table: every member reads every definition of the organization, a steward writes any definition with any field including is_public, is_template and report_type, an administrator deletes it, and no route reads is_public, shares a report or records a recipient. No adopted decision names the readers, the sharers or the meaning of the flag.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which offices may reproduce member and claim columns (member email, claimant and assignee identifiers, claim status and dates, dues amounts) in a free-form report, which columns are releasable at all, and what must be recorded and suppressed when a report returns them?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The execute route lets any caller whose role title is officer or above select the email and status of every member and the claim columns of its allowlist and join other registry tables, and records only a logger line; the role floor is a role title and no adopted decision names the offices, the releasable columns or the record to keep.

institutionalDecisions.question: Who may schedule a report for recurring delivery, which recipients (members, officers, addresses outside the union) and formats are allowed, who approves delivery of member or claim data outside the application, and what is the stop and audit rule for a schedule?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The scheduled report page collects recipients, a delivery method and an export format and posts them to routes that are generic CRUD over the reports table, which stores none of them, and the scheduled reports cron answers 501, so no delivery occurs and no adopted decision names the recipients, the approver or the audit rule that a real delivery would need.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which offices of a union may send a document for signature in its name and to which recipients, what identity proof binds a signer (a platform account, a verified e-mail address, a provider authentication) to the person whose name the audit trail states, what legal validity the union claims for a signature recorded in the platform or at a provider, and what makes the audit trail evidence (a sealed, verifiable record rather than an editable table)?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: Any authenticated user with an organization sends a document to typed signers through the provider the deployment configures or an internal stub that sends nothing, a signer is the user id the sender typed beside free-text name and e-mail address, a sender can sign as a named person and complete the document, and the audit trail is an editable table with an unused hash chain column that the service labels as generated for legal compliance. No source names the sending office, the identity proof or the validity basis.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which office of a union may connect, replace and remove its public social media accounts and hold their credentials, who may publish, schedule and delete a post in the union name and what approval, classification and member-consent check precedes publication, which analytics may members read, and how must the platform credentials be held and revoked?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: Any steward connects an organization account with administrative scopes and publishes at once to every connected account of a platform with no approval, credentials are stored as plain text and Meta and LinkedIn tokens are never revoked, a scheduled post is published immediately on three platforms, and analytics rows have no writer. No source names the connecting or publishing office, the approval step or the credential custody rule.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which office appoints, confirms and ends a steward of an organization, which of the fields held about a steward (type, unit and worksite coverage, tenure, appointer, work phone, personal phone, preferred contact method, availability notes, notes and the grievance a case-based assignment points at) may a member who is not a steward read, which may only stewards and officers read, and does an assignment row, the organization role title steward or the kernel mandate decide who acts as a steward?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The steward routes read steward_assignments at the member floor with every column and refuse every write through the CRUD governance list; the only code that inserts an assignment row is assignSteward in the steward assignment service, which no route calls, and the organization role steward lives on organization_members, which no steward route reads or changes. No source names the appointing office, the readable fields or the relation between an assignment row, a role title and a mandate.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which offices may read the satisfaction ratings that members give their representative (an individual representative, the ranking of every representative, the free text), is a rating published when only one or two members have answered, and does a member who asks to answer anonymously stay unidentifiable to the representative and to the stewards who read the figures?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The performance and ranking routes return per-representative averages at the steward floor with no minimum number of responses; the survey form tells the member that their name will not be visible to the representative, the route stores the anonymity flag on the row, and no query or route reads the flag. No source names the readers, a publication threshold or the anonymity rule.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which credential does an identity provider present to provision users into an organization (a long-lived bearer token held by whom, with what expiry and rotation), which identity attribute (userName, external id or subject) is the stable key of a provisioned person, what does a deprovision do (suspend, archive or delete the membership), which provider groups may confer which organization role, and who may read the provisioning log?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The SCIM users route authenticates a browser session and requires the administrator floor; the scim_configurations table with a bearer token, an expiry, a deprovision action and a user attribute mapping, and the scim_events_log table, exist, and the route reads neither; provisioning stores the userName string as the membership user id with the role member. No source names the credential, the key, the deprovision rule or the group-to-role mapping.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which of the keys held in the settings JSON of an organization (the per-capita rate and remittance day that set what it owes its parent body, the credit balance and renewal date that meter its use of metered features, the telephone number by which inbound text messages are attributed to it, branding, security policy and integration values) may the administrator of that organization write, which keys may only the platform operator or the parent body write, and which values must the software enforce when it saves them?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The organization settings route merges any object the administrator sends into the settings JSON with no key allow-list, and other code reads the same JSON as a remittance rate, a credit ledger and an inbound telephone number key; the page that saves multi-factor, session timeout and password policy values writes them to the same JSON and no code reads them to enforce anything. No source names which keys the administrator owns or which values are enforced.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which offices may read the security events of an organization (authentication, authorization, data access, configuration and suspicious activity, with the source address and user agent), may a person or a process other than the platform record or resolve an event, and how is an event shown not to have been authored or edited by the person it concerns?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The security events route is configured at the security manager floor for reads and writes, and the CRUD governance list denies the table, so every call answers 403; the only reader is the security dashboard page, which checks the security manager role and reads the table with SQL under a system context. No source names the readers, the authors or the integrity rule.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which office owns the support desk figures (ticket metrics, response and resolution time against a service-level target) and the storage figures (bytes used, quota and the cleanup of files nobody references) of an organization, which stored records are the source of each figure, and who may read them and trigger a cleanup that removes files?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The support metrics and SLA routes read and insert in_app_notifications rows and compute nothing; the storage usage and cleanup routes read and insert cms_media_library rows, sum no file size and delete no file; no route reads a ticket, service-level or storage quota table; getTicketMetrics and getSLAMetrics in the support service compute ticket and SLA figures from support_tickets and no route calls them. No source names the owner, the source records or the readers.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which office issues the tax documents an organization or a member relies on (the T4A and CRA export, the RL-1 slip, the T106 information return of related-party transactions, the receipt for a political contribution), from which stored records is each document computed, which readers may see the remittance ledger a document is drawn from, and may a member who is not an officer read the amounts the organization remits to its parent body?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The four tax paths read per_capita_remittances rows at the member floor and refuse every write because the table is READ_ONLY in the CRUD governance list; no route under these paths computes a slip, a return or a receipt, and the dashboard that links to the COPE receipt path expects a receipt for one member and year. The member floor, the ledger columns a member may read and the issuing office are named by no source.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which office holds the register of bargaining units and worksites (certification number, body and dates, chief steward, bargaining chair, composition, site manager contact), which of those fields may a member who is not a steward or officer read, who may create, change and archive a register row, and must every employer, worksite and steward identifier a row names be verified as belonging to the same organization?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The unit and worksite routes serve bargaining_units and worksites at the member read floor and the steward write floor with every column and no field projection; the identifiers they accept in a body (employer, worksite, chief steward, bargaining chair) are foreign keys with no check that the target belongs to the caller organization. No source names the register owner, the readable fields or the writers.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which offices may read and change the workers compensation claim of a member (injury, medical and prognosis detail, benefits paid, appeal dates, the union representative) and the premium assessment the organization receives from the board, does the representative who holds the member case decide who sees a claim, may a steward read the organization premium and payroll figures, and which board filings must the software itself submit?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The claim routes are configured at the steward floor and refused for every caller because wcb_claims is DENIED in the CRUD governance list; the assessment routes are served at the steward read and officer write floors with every premium, payroll and surcharge column. No source names the readers, the writers or the representative relation.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which office owns the testimonials and case studies shown on the public proof page, who approves a testimonial for publication and with what evidence of the speaker consent, may an administrator of one organization edit or delete content that every visitor sees, and may a signed-in member read a testimonial that is not approved or not public?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The testimonial item route is the generic CRUD factory over a table with no organization column, with orgScoped false, a member read floor and an administrator write floor, so the role is checked inside the caller own organization and the row is not; the table holds visibility and approvedAt columns that no read of the route consults, and the proof page describes its content as anonymized composites. No source names the owner, the approver or the consent evidence.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which office owns the key performance targets of an organization (who may create one, who may see its calculation and alert recipients, who may switch it off), which stored measurements are the source of each target (the data source and calculation a target declares), and in which direction is a threshold crossed (does a lower figure or a higher figure make a target critical)?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The target routes let an officer create a target with a free-form calculation record and a data source name and switch it on or off, and let any member read every target with its calculation, alert recipients and creator; the summary takes the current value from the latest analytics_metrics row whose metric type text equals the target metric type, applies no data source or calculation, and treats a value at or below a threshold as the worse state. No source names the owner, the source records or the direction rule.

institutionalDecisions.question: What is the disposition of the legacy compatibility and diagnostic routes (the /api/v2 mirror catch-all, the legacy tenant current wrapper and the Django auth-gate test): are they removed, answered with 410 Gone or 501 for every method, or kept for a stated period, and may a diagnostic route that forwards the session token to a backend ship in a production build?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The v2 catch-all answers every method with HTTP 200 and a deprecation body for any signed-in member, although the file that builds a 410 response (goneResponse) exists and is not called; the legacy tenant wrapper answers 200 with constant null values; the auth-gate test is a plain route that sends the session token to the configured Django address. No source states the sunset action, the replacement for each caller or the production position of the diagnostic.

institutionalDecisions.question: Who owns the CUPE vocabulary (case types, priority service-level hours, severity legal flags, role permission flags and the status transitions with the roles allowed to make them), is it a published institutional standard or a development default, how does a role named in it (chief steward, business agent) relate to the roles the application enforces, and who approves a change?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The vocabulary package holds hard-coded defaults marked version 0.1.0 whose generated timestamp is the time of each call; the routes serve them to any signed-in user as reference data with a public one-hour cache header, and no code found enforces the role or status flags. No source names the owner, the approval or the relation to the enforced roles.

institutionalDecisions.question: May a recording of a member or steward describing a claim be sent to an external speech service, on whose consent, under which processor agreement and in which region, is the recording or its transcript retained or discarded, who may transcribe, and is each transcription counted, limited and recorded?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The transcribe route (steward floor) sends the uploaded audio to the Azure speech service with no rate limit, entitlement, consent or audit record; the upload route (member floor) applies a rate limit and an entitlement check and sends the audio to an Azure OpenAI Whisper deployment, and no caller of it exists in the application. No source states the consent, the processor terms, the retention or the readers.

institutionalDecisions.question: Who may read the background queue health of Union Eyes (the pending and failed job counts, and the identifier and name of the recent failed tasks), which credential does the control plane present, and is a failed task name or error text an operator-only figure?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The queue status route accepts the shared AI service key in a header or any signed-in session with no role floor, returns the queue counts and the task id and name of recent failures, and answers an error with the error text. No source names the readers or separates the control plane credential from the AI service key.

institutionalDecisions.question: May an existing membership row be re-bound to a new sign-in identity because the e-mail address matches, who verifies that the address belongs to the person, may a row already bound to another identity be re-bound, and what record is kept of the re-binding?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The legacy branch of the organization choices route, entered when UE_CANONICAL_BOOTSTRAP_V2 is not 1, sets user_id on every membership row whose e-mail equals the caller e-mail when the caller has no membership, and on every row of the legacy user id of a profile with that e-mail, with no condition on the row current user id, no verified-address check and no audit record. No source names the linking authority.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which staff are eligible for a messages designation and which for a cases designation, is the eligibility rule the same for both scopes, and is the end of a lapsed designation recorded as an audited decision of a person or as a system event?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The grant route applies the case assignee eligibility test to a designation of either scope, while the message queue checks the conversation assignee roles when the designation is used; a lapsed designation is closed inside the next grant as revoked by system:expiry with no audit row. No source names the eligibility per scope or the record of expiry.

institutionalDecisions.question: On what consent, notice and retention does the institution keep a pseudonymous workbook and the names, roles and free-text notes of the people it describes, which payment processor may receive the workbook identifier, and when is an unclaimed workbook deleted?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The start route stores an optional consent object that no route reads, the checkout route sends the workbook identifier to Stripe in the redirect addresses and the session metadata, and the memory-holder routes store a display name and free-text notes of up to 4,000 characters about named people with no notice to them; no retention rule for an unclaimed or abandoned workbook is found. No source names the consent text, the processor terms or the deletion period.

institutionalDecisions.question: Who may claim a paid workbook into an organization, may any member of that organization (whatever their role) read, change and delete its memory holders and export it, and what authority does a person who holds only the workbook identifier keep over an unclaimed workbook?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The claim route binds the workbook to the organization that getOrganizationIdForUser resolves for the signed-in holder of the claim token; after the claim every member of that organization is treated as a peer with read and write authority (no role floor), and before the claim the workbook identifier alone authorizes reads and writes of the memory holders. No source names the claiming officer, the role floor for a peer or the pre-claim authority.

defectRegister.title: Route name advertises a business domain but the handler is the generic CRUD factory over organization_members; GET returns member roster rows under the advertised name and every write is refused.
The super-admin role repair route is the generic CRUD factory over organization_members; its documented repair does nothing and POST is refused.
The CLC organization analytics route is the generic CRUD factory over analytics_metrics, an OPERATIONAL table; any steward can create arbitrary analytics metric rows.

The mutation is audited through performAuditedOperation, which records intent and outcome in separate transactions from the effect. The manifest declares an atomic audit that the source does not show.
The route-coverage scanner misreports this operation: it marks CRUD reads as mutating, overstates the audit class, and misses the guard actually applied.
Billing history returns HTTP 200 with an empty list for a capability that has no storage; it must be an honest HTTP 501.
The target organization of a billing operation is caller-supplied and the guard checks only the caller role title, not authority over that organization.
A platform-wide read or operation is authorized by a role-title floor, not by a kernel decision or a platform-staff mandate.
Scheduled billing is latent: no scheduler calls it and the generator needs a session, so the route triggers work the system cannot run headless.
The report queries per_capita_remittances with no caller-organization predicate, so an organization administrator reads remittance data across organizations.
Administrator-only financial analytics is served with Cache-Control public, so shared caches may store it.
The organization audit log (user ids, resource ids, event details) is readable at the member role floor.
On the legacy path the AI-usage query reads audit_security rows for every organization with no organization predicate.
The organization directory returns member counts and contact name and email across organizations at a role-title floor.
PKI signing workflow state lives in a process-local Map; the signature_workflows table does not exist, so workflows are lost on restart and not shared across instances.
The representation protocol is a real, atomically audited, separation-of-duties flow that no capability names; ownership needs a Gate 0B.2 decision.
The three public-route lists disagree and the edge does not enforce them; routes that accept anonymous calls are absent from the lists.
The complete OpenAPI specification is served without authentication and is not on the public-route allowlist.
The version route exposes environment, host, deployment type, feature profile and image digests without authentication and is not on the public-route allowlist.
Tracking, click and unsubscribe handlers change state on GET (message log, campaign counters, preferences, consent records) although the manifest records them as read-only.
Anonymous telemetry is limited by a process-local in-memory limiter, which does not hold across instances.

The segment collection, segment item, segment execute and system settings routes advertise a business domain but are the generic CRUD factory over organization_members: GET returns member roster rows at the member floor, every write is refused, and nothing is segmented, executed or configured. A real member_segments table exists in the governance list and is not bound.

The update-role route is the generic CRUD factory over organization_members, a READ_ONLY table: GET returns member rows at the steward floor and POST is refused, so no role change can occur through it.

The analytics routes (claims, financial, executive, heatmap, comparative, dashboard, deadlines, clause statistics, trends, insights) are the generic CRUD factory over analytics_metrics, trend_analyses or insight_recommendations, which are OPERATIONAL. GET returns stored rows, not computed analytics, and any steward can insert arbitrary rows that are then served as analytics.

The platform user directory and activity feed select organization_members and organizations with no organization predicate at a platform_lead role title and return member name, email and role across organizations. Neither read is audited.

The cross-organization analytics route selects up to 1000 analytics_metrics rows through the global db handle inside a withRLSContext call that names no organization. The source does not show which rows tenant security returns, and the route is gated by a role title.

Member deactivation and removal revoke sessions, the platform-auth membership and the local row in separate stores. The audit record is atomic only with the local status update, and the route returns 502 when a step fails, leaving a partial state for a retry.
Agreement creation reads request.json() with no schema: only the status is checked, and every other field is inserted as supplied at a steward role-title floor.

AI grievance triage, clause reasoning and the copilot read any grievance in the organization for a steward role title. They do not check that the steward holds the case, so grievance content for cases the steward does not represent is sent to a model.

Routes that run enforceAISafety with grievance_legal, confidential or pension_financial data classes call the model with dataClass internal in the service layer. The two vocabularies disagree and the source shows no mapping between them.
Finance analysis and the pension projection, funding and trustee-summary routes read dues, arrears, remittances, trial-balance and pension data for an officer role title, with no financial mandate.

The employer-risk and insight-report GET handlers insert rows (employer_risk_scores, ai_insight_reports) through the global db handle and record the invocation with a separate auditLog event that is not committed with the row.
The classify, match-precedents, summarize and search routes call a model and write no audit event in the route handler or in the service that holds the AI call.
The classify route applies no AI feature gate and no AI safety check, although every sibling AI route applies both.
AI search and summarize return another organization's knowledge row when is_public is true, and no source says who may set the flag. Public cross-tenant data is not authorized by being public.
The semantic-search status GET counts every cba_clause and arbitration_precedents row across organizations through the global db handle with no organization predicate, at the member role floor.
The AI feedback GET returns every user's rating, comment and user id for a query id in the organization at the member role floor.
The AI ingest route indexes documents into a process-local Map, so an indexed document is lost on restart and not shared across instances, while the response reports status indexed.
The embedding cache statistics GET is gated by an organization administrator role title but reports platform-wide cache state.

Signing stores signatureValue ATTESTATION over a document-reference hash. The source says there is no cryptographic signature value, so verification cannot prove who signed or that content is unchanged.

The generic CRUD create copies the whole request body into the insert and the update strips only the primary key and organization column, so a caller can set status, author, approval, cost and provenance columns on every table whose route lists no blockedPatchFields; none of the Gate 0B.3 CRUD routes lists any.

The generic CRUD delete sets status archived on any table with a status column, but the break_status, negotiation_status, proposal_status and arbitration_status enums contain no archived value, so deletion of those records cannot succeed as designed and the failure is not shown by any source.

The break collection declares ownerColumn memberId, which references organization_members.id, and the factory compares it with the session user id for every caller; the item routes hold callers below steward to the same memberId comparison. The source does not show these are the same identifier, and on the collection staff are held to the same filter so no steward can review member breaks through it.

Break creation at the member floor does not force memberId from the session because the collection route declares an explicit ownerColumn, which sets the factory low-role mode to open, so a member can record a break, with its denial and compliance fields, for another member.
The KPI configuration read returns alert thresholds and the alertRecipients column to every member at the read floor.

Disconnecting a calendar requires the fixed administrator floor of the generic delete, so a member who connected their own calendar cannot disconnect it, and the delete removes the local row holding provider tokens without revoking the provider grant.
The bulk-import route is the generic CRUD factory over organization_members, a READ_ONLY table: GET returns the member roster to staff and POST is refused, so nothing is imported.
The precedent citations, documents and search routes are the generic CRUD factory over arbitration_decisions: they return and change decision rows and serve no citations, documents or search results.

arbitration_decisions has no organization column, so the library routes return every decision row to every organization whatever isPublic or accessRestrictions say, and the row-level-security policy admits any tenant context.
The library delete uses the fixed administrator floor of the generic factory and hard-deletes the row, so an organization administrator can delete a decision that every organization reads.

A steward can insert an insight_recommendations row through the generic factory with an aiReferenceId, confidence score and recommendations of their choosing, and the row is then served as an AI insight.
The weekly summary records an AI invocation naming model analytics-engine and stores confidenceScore 0.83 and fixed recommendation text for a computation that counts events and runs no model.
The synchronized accounting invoice read returns customer names, balances and amounts to every member at the read floor, ahead of any financial mandate.
The invoice create route is the generic factory over external_invoices, a READ_ONLY table: every POST is refused, so the advertised invoice creation does not exist.
The arbitration collection and item routes read and write arbitration rows for any steward of the organization, accept any grievanceId in the body and do not check that the steward holds the case.

bargaining_proposals has no organization column, so the generic factory adds no tenant predicate to reads, updates or deletes and the create accepts any negotiationId; isolation rests only on a row-level-security policy this tranche cannot show is applied.
The batch invoicing route selects every active subscription across all organizations and generates an invoice for each at an organization administrator role title, returning every organization id.
The invoice replay route selects the invoice and its line items by id with no organization predicate at a steward role floor, so one organization can read another organization invoice.

Invoice generation, invoice replay and trial expiry declare an atomic service audit, but invoice generation records auditLog after its inserts outside a transaction, replay records a separate access event, and trial expiry writes no audit record.

The billing validation route records only application log events and labels ordinary validation failures unauthorized_access or auth_failed, so security monitoring cannot tell an attack from a wrong currency.

The observability sweep writes alert rules, executions and notifications through the module-level db handle and its audit record through the sweep transaction handle; the source shows no proof that they commit together.
The audits list presents audit-log rows as audit engagements and invents status, findings 0 and hasReport false for every row.
The audit item route returns the complete audit_logs row, with details and any recorded address and agent, to an officer role floor with no redaction by reader.

The audits routes read the audit_security audit_logs table, while persistAtomicAudit writes the domains infrastructure audit_logs table, so the routes do not show the audit records the atomic writers produce.

The bargaining-notes GET returns timeline, statistics and session-type results before the visibleToUserId confidentiality filter is applied, and the timeline returns the title of every note of an agreement whatever its confidentiality level.

The bargaining-note item GET and PATCH are the generic factory: a member reads any note by id, including restricted and confidential notes the collection route withholds, and an update skips the agreement check the collection create applies.

Tentative agreement creation verifies the parent negotiation but stores relatedProposalIds and relatedClauseId without verifying that the proposals or clause belong to that negotiation or organization.
Negotiation and tentative-agreement reads sit at the member floor and ignore confidentialityLevel, so strike-vote results, cost ceilings and costed agreements reach every member.

The trial-expiry route passes a payment-method checker that always returns false, so every expired trial of the organization is cancelled whether or not a payment method exists, at a steward role floor.
The send-invoice route generates and stores an invoice and returns it; nothing is delivered, whatever the route name advertises.

Subscription commercial terms are readable at the member floor, pause, resume, invoice generation and trial expiry sit at the steward floor, and update and cancel sit at the secretary_treasurer role title, a union finance role; no source names the office with contract authority.
calculateMetrics stores claim identifiers in the metric metadata and the metrics GET returns that metadata to every member at the member floor.

The metrics routes resolve the organization once in the route wrapper and again in the action through getOrganizationIdForUser, and the action ignores the first, so a user with more than one membership may write to an organization other than the session organization.

The derived case metrics and the weekly summary count pilot telemetry events and present them as case figures; open cases are created minus closed events and overdue cases are breached minus closed events, with no case table read.

The break compliance report returns per-member denied, missed and flagged counts to any steward while the generic break route holds a member to their own rows, so the report is authorized more broadly than the records it is computed from.

The realtime alerts route returns the raw triggerData of alert executions, with SLA-risk, ingestion-failure and payment-failure counts, to every member under a case-suite entitlement, with no redaction and no named reader.

The Google and Microsoft authorization routes pass the session user id as the OAuth state and the callbacks compare the returned state with that same id, and accept a callback with no state at all, so the state is neither unguessable nor single-use and gives no protection against a forged callback.

The provider callbacks are GET handlers that exchange a code and insert or update the connection row holding the provider tokens, and neither the callback nor the member-floor wrapper writes an audit record for the connection, so a state-changing GET leaves no audit evidence.

encryptCalendarToken returns the token unencrypted when no encryption key is configured outside production, and decryptCalendarToken returns any value without the encryption prefix as it is, so a database written without the key holds provider tokens in clear text and never fails.
The connection collection and item reads select the whole external_calendar_connections row, so the stored accessToken and refreshToken values are returned to the browser of the connection owner.

A steward can create or update a connection through the generic factory with any provider, providerAccountId, accessToken and refreshToken, stored as supplied and unencrypted, and an update can reassign userId, so the OAuth flow and the token encryption can be bypassed and a connection can be handed to another user.

The connection sync route selects the connection by id and organization only, with no userId predicate and no role above organization membership, so any member can run an import or export through another member provider account.

The sync route proves that the local calendar and event are in the organization but not that the caller owns a personal calendar or may read a personal event, so a member can import into or export from another member personal calendar.

The sync records intent and outcome through performAuditedOperation around an external provider call, and the connection update runs inside that operation without the audit record; the record is not committed with the state change.

The calendar item route supplies lockedAuthCheck to reject another member personal calendar, but the factory invokes it only when beforeUpdate or mergeJsonColumns is configured and never on delete, and the route configures neither, so a steward can still update or delete another member personal calendar.

The calendar events routes filter events by calendar id and organization or by organization alone and never consult calendars.isPersonal or ownerId, which calendar_events does not carry, so a member reads events of another member personal calendar through calendars/[id]/events and staff read every personal event through calendar/events.

Event create and update store a caller-supplied calendarId without verifying that the calendar belongs to the organization or is visible to the caller; the foreign key checks only that a calendar row exists.

No table of the CBA intelligence dataset has an organization column and none of the services filters by organization, so every organization reads, and every administrator or steward writes, one shared dataset; nothing in the source states which organizations may read it or who curates it.

The agreement list, item and export reads apply a review status filter only when the caller supplies one, so extracted agreements, wage adjustments and clauses that are pending, rejected or superseded are returned as the dataset.

Source registration and update, ingestion, seeding and extraction require only an organization administrator role floor, yet they create and change the dataset every organization reads and call external services at the platform expense, so the administrator of any one organization can curate platform-wide data; no source names the platform staff mandate.

A steward of any organization can approve, reject or supersede an extracted record, which sets the review status every organization sees, and the decision records the reviewer role as the literal steward whatever the caller role is.

Extraction, ingestion runs and source seeding declare an atomic service audit, but they record intent and outcome through performAuditedOperation around many separate statements and an external provider call, so the audit record is not committed with the state change.

The benchmark GET inserts a cba_intel_benchmark_snapshots row when save=true, recording the caller user id, and the route and the service write no audit record, so a state-changing GET is both mislabelled as a read and unaudited.

The snapshot history is selected by target agreement only and returns the computedBy user id of whoever saved each snapshot, so a steward of one organization reads the user ids of stewards of other organizations.

The export route asks the service for 10000 rows but listAgreements clamps the limit to 100, so the CSV advertised as an export of the agreements holds at most the first 100 rows and says nothing about it.

Source registration accepts any URL for the base, API, feed and terms addresses, and the ingestion adapters fetch the discovered document URLs from the server with no host allow-list or private-address check, so an administrator can make the platform request internal addresses.

The moderation step returns not flagged when OPENAI_API_KEY is unset and, when the moderation request fails, returns a flagged result with the reason Safety system unavailable that sendMessage then ignores and proceeds, although the code comments call the failure closed; a member message reaches the model unmoderated whenever moderation is absent or down.

The moderation step posts the member message text directly to api.openai.com with a provider key, outside @nzila/ai-sdk which the same file names as the only route for AI calls, so the data-class, budget and audit controls of the AI control plane do not apply to that call.
