releaseDisposition.actualExposure: When UE_MEMBER_DUES_PAYMENTS=1 a member who calls POST /api/portal/dues/pay repeatedly (a double click, a retry after a timeout, two tabs) gets a new pending dues_transactions row and a new Stripe PaymentIntent for the full outstanding balance on each call, because the idempotency key is derived from the new payment id and no existing pending payment is looked up; settlement locks only the paid row and credits the ledger by that row amount without comparing it with the balance then owed.

potentialImpact.description: A member who confirms two of the intents is charged twice for the same dues and the ledger is credited twice, driving the balance below zero (balance_after is the prior balance minus the amount with no floor), so money is taken from a member beyond what they owe and the union carries a refund that no route can issue.

existingContainment.summary: The initiation answers 501 unless the deployment sets UE_MEMBER_DUES_PAYMENTS=1, and settlement of a payment is a single guarded update from pending, so a given pending payment cannot settle twice.

evidence.quote: throw ApiError.notImplemented('Member dues payment is not enabled in this deployment')

releaseDisposition.blockingCondition: A deployment sets UE_MEMBER_DUES_PAYMENTS=1 so that members can pay dues through the application; the route then creates one charge-capable intent per call for the entire balance and can collect the same dues more than once.
releaseDisposition.justification: The flag keeps the route at 501 today, so no member can be charged now, but the defect is in the initiation and settlement logic and not in a configuration choice: the moment the flag is enabled every repeat call yields another full-balance intent and nothing in the settlement path stops the second payment from crediting the ledger past zero, so enabling member dues payments is blocked until the repeat and overpayment paths are closed.

defectRegister.title: POST /api/portal/dues/pay commits the pending dues_transactions row and its dues.payment_initiated audit row in one transaction and only then calls the Stripe API outside any transaction; the later update that stores processor_payment_id and the update that sets the row to cancelled after a processor failure are separate transactions with no audit row, and the cancellation is wrapped in a catch that discards its own failure, so an initiation can be audited for a payment whose provider call never happened and the cancelled state is not audited.

POST /api/portal/dues/pay sends the organization id and the member user id in the PaymentIntent metadata to Stripe through the platform-managed Stripe client (lib/stripe delegates to a platform client; the route holds no per-organization processor configuration): no source names the merchant account that receives union dues, whether it is the union or the platform operator, or the member consent for the disclosure, and the route holds no per-organization processor configuration.

The generic CRUD routes at /api/precedents/[id] are configured orgScoped true over arbitration_precedents, whose organization column is named source_organization_id and which has no organizationId, no status and no userId or memberId: the factory adds the tenant predicate only for an organizationId column and the low-role guard holds a caller to own rows only for a userId or memberId column, so GET (member), PATCH (steward) and DELETE (administrator) address any precedent row of any organization by id, whatever its sharing_level and shared_with_org_ids.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: A member of any organization can GET, a steward can PATCH and an administrator can DELETE /api/precedents/<id> for any arbitration_precedents row: orgScoped true adds a tenant predicate only when the table has an organization column, and this table is keyed by source_organization_id, so the factory query filters on the id alone and the low-role guard finds no owner column to hold a member to.

potentialImpact.description: A precedent another organization contributed, whatever its sharing level (the column defaults to federation and the sector statistics treat private as excluded), is readable, rewritable (including its sharing level, shared-with list, document links and source organization) and permanently deletable with its tags and citations by users of other organizations once its id is known.

releaseDisposition.justification: The route has no tenant predicate and no sharing test, the table carries a sharing level and a shared-with list that no read or write route applies, and a row-level-security policy on source_organization_id applies only on a connection role that is subject to it, which the source does not establish for these reads and writes; a cross-tenant read and write of institutional case material is not contained by that, so the route blocks release.

defectRegister.title: PATCH /api/precedents/[id] copies the request body into the arbitration_precedents update, so a steward can change sharing_level, shared_with_org_ids, is_parties_anonymized (turning the anonymization of the parties off), the document links and the source_organization_id itself with no sharing authority, no review and no record of the previous value; the audit row lists only the changed field names.

DELETE /api/precedents/[id] permanently deletes the arbitration_precedents row (the table has no status column, so the factory hard-deletes) and the foreign keys on precedent_tags and precedent_citations cascade, so the tags and the citation history of the precedent are destroyed with no soft delete, no withdrawal rule and an audit row that keeps only the row id and the changed field names.

GET /api/precedents (list, issue type, most cited) and POST /api/precedents/search select every column of arbitration_decisions at the member and steward floor, including the grievor name, the panel members, the full text and the embedding, and apply no condition on is_public or access_restrictions, so a decision recorded as not public or carrying an access restriction is returned and searched (the search also matches inside the full text) exactly like a public one; the table has no organization column and the library is shared across organizations.

GET /api/precedents passes parseInt of the limit and page query values to the list, most-cited and issue-type queries with no maximum, no minimum and no NaN check, so a caller can request an arbitrarily large page, a negative offset or a NaN limit, and the sortBy value is taken from the query string; the statistics mode counts the whole library.

POST /api/precedents/search validates only that the query is a string of at most 500 characters and that filters is a record of unknown values, then builds %query% LIKE conditions over the title, case number, summary, headnote and full text without escaping the percent and underscore wildcards, and casts the filter values to the tribunal and precedent value enums without validating them, so an invalid enum value reaches the database as a 500 and a broad pattern scans the whole text column.

POST /api/precedents inserts the typed decision into the library that every organization reads, with the full text, grievor and parties as typed, is_public defaulting to true, no source or import provenance and no organization on the row (the organization appears only in the audit row), after a single role-title check (content_manager) and with no review, redaction or consent step.

PUT /api/precedents/jurisdiction-preferences selects the caller row and then updates or inserts it, but member_jurisdiction_preferences declares no unique index on user_id and organization_id, so two concurrent first saves insert two rows and GET returns an arbitrary one of them; includeNational and autoApply are written as typed with no boolean check, and no precedent route reads the preferences (only the console components apply them in the browser), so the saved preference filters nothing on the server.

GET /api/profile/roles is the generic CRUD list over the profiles table (readRole member, orgScoped true) although profiles has no organization column, so the tenant predicate is not added, and the low-role guard restricts only callers below steward to their own row: a steward or higher of any organization receives every profile of the platform with email, membership tier, payment provider, Stripe customer and subscription ids, Whop ids, plan dates and credit counters.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: A steward or any higher role of any organization calls GET /api/profile/roles and receives every row of the profiles table: each user email, membership tier, payment provider, Stripe customer and subscription ids, Whop ids, plan dates and credit counters; orgScoped true is a no-op because profiles has no organization column and the low-role guard releases a caller at steward and above from the own-row restriction.

potentialImpact.description: Contact addresses and payment-provider identifiers of every user of the platform, across all organizations, are listed to the stewards of any one organization, in pages of up to 100 rows, which exposes customer billing identity and supports phishing and account-linking attacks.

releaseDisposition.justification: A steward is a routine office of every local, the role floor restricts the reader to staff of some organization and not to the owner of the profile, the table has no organization column to scope by, and the profiles row-level-security policy depends on a runtime role the source does not establish for this read; a reachable cross-tenant list of personal and billing identifiers is not contained by a staff role, so the route blocks release.

defectRegister.title: The route named profile/roles lists billing profiles (membership tier, payment provider and credits) and holds no role, role assignment or permission data, so a client that expects a role list receives subscription records; its POST is configured at the steward floor but profiles is READ_ONLY in the CRUD governance table, so every POST is refused with 403 after the role check, and no route assigns a role.

GET /api/profile/me returns isSuccess true with the message Profile retrieved successfully and data null when the profile query fails or times out: getProfileByUserId catches the lookup error and returns null, so a database failure and a user who has no profile are indistinguishable from each other, and the caller is told the profile was retrieved.

GET /api/reconciliation/process?runId= checks the caller finance:view mandate in the caller own organization and then returns getReconciliationRun(runId), whose query is .where(eq(reconciliationRuns.id, runId)) with no organization condition and which is read through the shared db handle, so an officer of any organization with the commercial_reporting entitlement reads any other organization reconciliation run (totals, variance, counts, run-by user, billing period) by id.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: An officer of any organization that holds the commercial_reporting entitlement calls GET /api/reconciliation/process?runId=<uuid> and receives the reconciliation run with that id whichever organization owns it: the route checks the caller own financial mandate and then calls getReconciliationRun(runId), whose query filters on the run id alone.

potentialImpact.description: Another organization run record (period, invoice and payment counts, invoice and payment totals in CAD, variance, run-by user id and the billing period id) is returned to a caller outside that organization once its run id is known, with no organization predicate to refuse it.

releaseDisposition.justification: The mandate check proves only that the caller holds the finance:view duty in their own organization, the entitlement gate restricts the route to organizations that bought commercial_reporting but not to the owner of the run, the run id is a uuid supplied by the caller, and the service query has no organization condition; a reachable cross-tenant read is not contained by an identifier being hard to guess, so the route blocks release.

defectRegister.title: The reconciliation service (runReconciliation, resolveException, getReconciliationRun, listExceptions, requireReconciliation) imports the shared db handle and opens its own db.transaction without a tenant context, so the organization predicates written in each query (and absent from getReconciliationRun and requireReconciliation) are the only boundary unless the connection role is itself subject to row-level security, which the route files do not establish; the mandate check in the route runs in a separate withRLSContext transaction that the service does not join.

runReconciliation writes the run, matches and exceptions in db.transaction but calls auditLog (the application audit logger, which does not take the transaction handle) inside it, and resolveException updates the exception and then calls auditLog after the update committed, so the audit event is a separate write: a failed audit of a resolution or write-off leaves the status changed without the record (and in legacy mode the logger logs and swallows a database failure), and a run that later rolls back can leave its audit event behind.

POST /api/reconciliation/process inserts a new reconciliation_runs row and fresh exception rows on every call for the same period (no uniqueness, no supersede or correction of an earlier run), stores the billingPeriodId from the body without checking that the period belongs to the organization, and requireReconciliation(billingPeriodId), the guard that decides whether a period may be closed, filters the runs by period id alone with limit 1 and no order, so a run of one organization (or any earlier run) can satisfy the closure guard; the only caller of that guard is closeBillingPeriod, which no route calls.

runReconciliation records a fee_settlement match for each fee event that has a settlement batch id by copying the fee amount as both the source and the target amount with a variance of 0.00, without reading any settlement batch amount, so these matches are always reported as matched; it sums payments whose status is refunded into the payment total as if received; and the exception types duplicate_payment, missing_fee_event and orphaned_refund that the schema defines are never created, so the run reports totals and exception counts that do not test duplicates, missing fees or refunds.

POST /api/reconciliation/resolve sets an exception to resolved or written_off with the typed notes (an empty string is accepted) and the resolver id, and changes no invoice, payment or ledger row, so a write-off removes the exception from the open list without any financial effect or evidence; the service does not compare the resolver with the user who ran the reconciliation, no second approver is required, and the mandate check passes no participants to the segregation-of-duties rule.

GET /api/reconciliation/bank lists the reconciliation runs of the organization and GET /api/reconciliation/upload lists reconciliation exceptions; neither receives, parses or matches a bank statement (the upload route comment says the intake is reserved for future work), and no route records a bank transaction, so the paths named for bank reconciliation reconcile platform invoices and payments only.

GET /api/reconciliation/bank returns every run of the organization with no limit, and GET /api/reconciliation/upload splits the status query value on commas and casts it to the exception status enum without validation (and returns every matching exception unpaged), so an invalid status value reaches the database as an enum error and the lists grow without bound.

GET /api/rewards/export has no role check: after a session and the organization lookup it selects by organization alone and returns as a CSV download every award (recipient and issuer user ids, reason text), every wallet ledger row (user id, event type, credits, balance, memo) and every budget envelope of the organization to any member, while the wallet and redemption routes hold a member to their own rows.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: Any signed-in member of an organization calls GET /api/rewards/export?type=ledger, awards or budgets and receives a CSV of every row of the organization: all members user ids with their credit amounts, balances and memos, every award with recipient, issuer and reason, and every budget envelope; the route resolves the organization from the session and applies no role test and no relation between a row and the caller.

potentialImpact.description: Colleagues learn what each member earned and spent, the free-text reason and memo attached to each award and ledger entry, who recognised whom and the program budgets, which the wallet and redemption routes hold to the member own rows and which no source says members may see.

releaseDisposition.justification: The only guards are a session and an organization membership at any role, the queries select by organization alone and return the whole table as a download, and the sibling wallet and redemption routes show the intended own-row boundary; the data is personal to each member and the audience is undecided, so a signed-in member reaches every colleague record today and the route blocks release.

defectRegister.title: The CSV writer of GET /api/rewards/export quotes only values that contain a comma, a quote or a newline and does not neutralise a leading equals, plus, minus or at sign, so a free-text award reason or ledger memo that begins with a formula is written verbatim and is evaluated when an administrator opens the file in a spreadsheet.

GET /api/rewards/export returns the whole awards, ledger or budgets table of the organization in one response with no limit or date range, and records nothing about who exported what: the route writes no audit row and sits under no wrapper that does, so a bulk disclosure of member wallet data leaves no trace.

The anniversary task of POST /api/rewards/cron selects every organization member whose join date has today month and day and, for each, creates and issues a new Work Anniversary recognition award (credits applied by issueAward) with no check for an award already made for that member and year and no uniqueness on recipient, award type and date in recognition_awards, so the same call repeated on the same day, a scheduler retry or an overlapping run awards and credits the members again; the awards and credits are created in two separate transactions per member.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: The scheduler holder of CRON_SECRET calls POST /api/rewards/cron (task anniversaries or all); for every active organization the task selects every member whose join date falls on today and creates and issues a new Work Anniversary award with its credit amount, with no record or constraint that the award was already made, so a second call on the same day, a scheduler retry or an overlapping run awards and credits the same members again.

potentialImpact.description: Members receive the anniversary credits two or more times, the wallet ledger and program budget are charged each time, duplicate recognition awards appear in the member history and the export, and the credits are redeemable for provider goods, so a retry converts directly into spendable value.

existingContainment.summary: Only a caller with the cron secret reaches the task, and an anniversary award is issued only for an organization that has configured an automated Work Anniversary award type, which the route does not create.

evidence.quote: logger.warn('[Automation] No anniversary award type found', { orgId });

releaseDisposition.blockingCondition: An organization configures an automated Work Anniversary award type with a credit amount and the scheduler calls the cron route more than once on a day on which a member has an anniversary (a retry, an overlapping run, two schedulers, or a manual call).
releaseDisposition.justification: The route reaches no one without the shared secret and no award is made until an organization configures the automated type, so the harm is conditional; once an organization has done so, any repeat of the call on an anniversary day creates and credits a second award because recognition_awards has no uniqueness on recipient, type and day, and the credits are spendable, so the repeat path blocks release for any organization that uses anniversary awards.

defectRegister.title: The scheduled task of POST /api/rewards/cron loads the active scheduled automation rules of each organization, logs each one and increments processed without evaluating any schedule or issuing any award (the source comment calls it a placeholder), so the response reports rules processed for work that was not done.

The expiration task of POST /api/rewards/cron e-mails members whose earn ledger rows have an expires_at inside the next 7, 14 and 30 days (three overlapping windows run on every call, so a row expiring in 5 days is selected in all three), summing the earned credits of those rows and ignoring any spending; the call sites that write earn rows pass no expiresAt and no code was found that writes an expire entry, so today the task selects nothing and reports success with zero notifications, and once an expiry is set it would mail the same member up to three times per run with no sent record and with a credit count that does not reflect what was spent.

POST /api/rewards/cron returns success true with HTTP 200 for any task value (an unknown task executes nothing and returns an empty executed list), embeds a per-organization failure as an entry inside a successful response (processAnniversaryAwards returns success false with the error object instead of throwing, and a rejected organization is serialised as an Error object that JSON renders as empty), and wraps the expiration result, whose own success flag may be false, in the same success true, so a scheduler that checks the status code cannot see a failed run.

The proxy requires the x-cron-secret header for /api/rewards/cron and compares it with the CRON_SECRET value using !==, and the route then requires the same secret again in an Authorization bearer header (compared in constant time), so a scheduler must send the secret in two transports, a secret query parameter is documented in the route comment but not read, and the GET handler has no secret check of its own and depends on the proxy alone.

processAnniversaryAwards computes calculateAnniversaryCredits(yearsOfService) into a variable that is never used (the credit amount issued is the award type default), so a service-based credit scale is implied but not applied, and the reason text stored on every award and shown to the member reads with followed by the organization UUID instead of the organization name.

The rewards cron route and the wallet, redemption, automation, award and notification services import the shared db handle (and the cron route lists every active organization through it and runs raw SQL on organization_members) without a tenant context, and the wallet and redemption routes are wrapped by withRoleAuth, which sets no row-level-security context, so the organization and user predicates written in each query are the only boundary unless the connection role is itself subject to row-level security, which the route files do not establish.

Each anniversary award commits its create audit row in the award transaction and its issue audit row in a second transaction, but the cron run as a whole (organizations covered, members awarded, failures, warnings e-mailed) is written to no audit row, a failure between the two transactions leaves an approved award that is never issued and is not retried, and the expiration e-mails that leave the application are not recorded anywhere beyond a log line.

GET /api/rewards/redemptions validates the status query value against pending, ordered, fulfilled, cancelled and refunded (the cancellable states initiated and pending_payment are not in the list) and then never passes it to listUserRedemptions, so the filter has no effect and a member cannot ask for the redemptions that they are allowed to cancel; hasMore is the page length equal to the limit.

GET /api/rewards/redemptions returns the whole reward_redemptions row of each of the caller redemptions (listUserRedemptions uses findMany with no column list), including providerPayloadJson, which holds the shop provider checkout payload and the cancellation reason, so provider-side identifiers are returned to the member browser.

POST /api/rewards/redemptions parses the body with initiateRedemptionSchema into a variable that is never used and then cancels the redemption named by the id query value (refunding the credits), so a client that posts a new redemption receives a cancellation or a missing-id error, the schema validates fields that are ignored, and the cancel does not tell the shop provider that the checkout it may already hold has been cancelled.

GET /api/rewards/wallet reads the balance (the latest ledger row by created_at) and the ledger page in separate statements, so a ledger write between them returns a balance that does not match the page, takes limit and offset from parseInt of the query string without a NaN or negative check, and reports hasMore as the page length equal to the limit.

The report definition reads (the collection, the item and every path that is a copy of them) are the generic factory read at a member floor over the reports table: the table has no owner column the factory uses and the routes declare no ownerColumn, so any member of the organization receives every report definition of the organization, including definitions written by other users and definitions whose is_public flag is false, each with its whole config JSON that names data sources, fields and filter values, and no route under /api/reports reads is_public, so the flag restricts nothing.

The report definition writes store the config JSON from the request body as written: the column is an untyped notNull jsonb, no schema bounds its size or depth, and nothing at save time applies the contract of the report executor (a data source id of its registry, registry field ids, its filter operators, its allowed joins) or the allowlist of the execute route, so a definition that names an unknown source, a refused operator or a join to any table is stored and returned as a success that a later run would refuse or misread.

The /api/reports/[id]/execute and /api/reports/[id]/run routes are the same generic crudRoutes configuration over the reports table as the item route: neither imports ReportExecutor, reads a source table or loads the config of the report into an engine, so a GET answers the stored definition row (not a result), a PATCH rewrites the definition (including run_count and last_run_at, which no route ever advances) and answers success, and a DELETE at the administrator floor hard-deletes the report itself, so a caller or client that believes it is running or removing a run removes the report definition.

The /api/reports/[id]/share route is the same generic crudRoutes configuration over the reports table as the item route: it has no recipient, link, grant or share column, sends nothing and checks nothing, a PATCH that sets is_public true or false only stores a flag that no route reads, and a DELETE at the administrator floor, the natural verb to revoke a share, hard-deletes the whole report, so a share request is answered with success while nothing is shared, and a revocation destroys the report.

potentialImpact.description: A member, including one who is the subject of a grievance the steward handles, reads the personal telephone number and availability notes of every steward and the grievance each case-based assignment is linked to; a steward who gave a work number to members has also given every member a personal number and free-text notes, and the grievance link reveals which member or case a steward is assigned to.

existingContainment.summary: The factory adds an organization predicate from the session organization, so only the rows of the caller own organization are read; nothing narrows them to a steward, an officer, a coverage area or a set of permitted fields, so the exposure is every steward row of the organization to every member.

releaseDisposition.justification: The routes serve personal contact data and free-text notes about a union representative, and a grievance link, to every authenticated member at the lowest role floor with no field projection; the tenant predicate keeps other organizations out but does not limit a same-organization reader, and no source establishes that members are the intended audience of the personal phone, the notes or the grievance link, so the read blocks release until the institution names the readers and the permitted fields.

defectRegister.title: The stewards and stewards/[id] routes are crudRoutes over steward_assignments: GET returns assignment rows, POST, PATCH and DELETE are refused with 403 because the governance list holds the table read-only, no other route appoints, confirms or ends a steward, and the only code that inserts an assignment row is assignSteward in the steward assignment service (a grievance assignment that sets the type to steward, writes no audit record and bumps a caseload counter on the separate stewards table) which no route calls, so the route names promise a steward directory with appointment and the source offers a read of per-case assignment rows and no way to create the directory.

The stewards collection and item routes configure writeRole steward over steward_assignments and the item route exports PATCH and DELETE with no blocked fields; the only thing that stops a steward from creating, rewriting or archiving any steward assignment (type, appointer, tenure, coverage, notes) is the presence of steward_assignments in the READ_ONLY list of the CRUD governance file, so a role title at the steward floor would become the authority to appoint stewards the moment that list changes.

The survey form tells the member that submitting anonymously means their name will not be visible to their representative, and the submit route stores isAnonymous on the survey row, but no query, service function or route reads the flag: the survey row keeps member_id and the rating and the free text whatever the flag says, the representative performance and ranking routes aggregate anonymous and named responses together, and a representative with one completed survey is returned that one response as an average, so an anonymous response is not anonymous to a steward who knows which claim the representative handled.

GET /api/satisfaction/lro/<lroId> returns the six rating averages, the overall average and the recommend rate of any representative id the steward types in, and GET /api/satisfaction/rankings returns and ranks every representative of the organization who has a completed survey, at the steward floor, with no minimum number of responses, no check that the id is a representative of the organization or the caller, no control over which steward may read the performance of which representative, and no read audit.

getLroPerformance turns a null average into zero (n = parseFloat(v ?? 0)) and computes the overall average as the mean of six values that may all be zero, so GET /api/satisfaction/lro/<lroId> for an id that is not a representative, or that has no completed survey in the organization, answers 200 with totalSurveys 0, six averages of 0, an overall average of 0 and a recommend rate of 0, which reads as a representative rated 0 out of 5 and not as no data.

POST /api/satisfaction (described in its header as an administrator action and in its OpenAPI text as creating a survey for a closed claim) is configured at the steward floor and selects only memberId and assignedTo from the claim: it never reads the claim status, so a survey can be created for an open claim, and when the claim has no assignedTo the lroId in the body is accepted as any string with no check that it names a representative of the organization, so a survey can be created that asks the member to rate a person who did not handle the claim.

GET /api/satisfaction passes only the session user id to getPendingSurveys, which filters satisfaction_surveys on member_id and status pending with no organization predicate and returns the whole rows, so a person who is a member of two organizations receives the pending surveys of both (claim id, representative id, sent time) whichever organization the session is acting in.

The SCIM 2.0 users route authenticates only a browser session at the administrator floor (withApi auth required, minRole admin) and reads neither scim_configurations (bearer token, token hash, expiry, enabled flag, deprovision action, attribute mapping) nor scim_events_log, so an identity provider that presents the long-lived bearer token the schema describes cannot call it, no token is issued, checked, expired or rotated by any route, no SCIM provisioning event is logged, and the route offers only list and create with no get, replace, patch or delete of a user, no groups and no service provider configuration, so a deprovision cannot be sent at all.

GET /api/scim/v2/<organizationId>/Users selects every organization_members row of the organization with no deleted_at and no status condition, slices the page in memory after loading the whole roster, and maps active to member.status equal to active alone, so a member who was removed (deleted_at set) while the status column still reads active is listed and reported as an active user with name and e-mail address, a count that is not a number (count=abc) makes the slice end NaN and the page empty, and a count of zero or less is accepted.

POST /api/scim/v2/<organizationId>/Users inserts an organization_members row whose user_id is the userName string from the body (the membership key that getUserRoleInOrganization matches against the session user id), with the e-mail taken from the body, the role fixed to member and the status active immediately: the identity provider subject is never read, the person does not accept, the userName may be any string including the identifier of an existing user of another organization (who is then made an active member of this one), and a provisioned person whose session user id differs from the userName string can never match the row, while a removed member with the same user id answers 409 as an existing user.

The SCIM create route reads the body with an unguarded request.json() and a type cast instead of a schema: malformed JSON or an emails value that is not an array raises a plain error that withApi answers as a 500, a userName that is not a string passes the presence check and reaches the insert, and no length or format bound is applied to userName, name or e-mail.

PUT /api/settings/organization merges whatever object the administrator sends as body.settings, with no key allow-list and no value validation, into the organizations.settings JSON that other code reads as authority: services/clc/per-capita-calculator reads settings.perCapitaRate (an organization with a rate of 0 or less is skipped) and settings.remittanceDay to compute the per-capita amount an organization with a parent owes that parent, lib/services/entitlements reads settings.credits and settings.nextCreditRenewal as the credit balance that checkEntitlement tests before a credit-requiring AI feature, and the twilioPhoneNumber key attributes inbound text messages, so an organization administrator can set their own remittance rate and day, credit balance and renewal date directly, and the audit row lists only the names of the fields written (settings, name, shortName, provinceTerritory), never a value.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: An administrator of any organization (minRole admin) sends PUT /api/settings/organization with {"settings":{"perCapitaRate":"0.01","credits":1000000}}: the route merges the object into the stored settings JSON of the session organization in a tenant transaction and commits an organization.settings_update audit row that names the field settings but not the values, and the per-capita calculator and the entitlement check read those keys back on their next call.

potentialImpact.description: An organization administrator can lower or zero the per-capita rate (a rate of 0 removes the organization from the monthly remittance run, a low rate shrinks the amount computed as owed to its parent body) and can set the credit balance and renewal date that the entitlement check reads, so the parent body and the platform operator, who are not the writer, receive an amount the software computed from a value the payer wrote; the audit row does not record the values, so the change cannot be reconstructed.

existingContainment.summary: The caller must hold the administrator role and the update is scoped to the organization id of the session, so one organization cannot write another organization row; nothing limits which keys the administrator writes or which organization reads them for billing and remittance.

releaseDisposition.justification: The remittance amount lands on a party other than the writer (the parent body that the per-capita calculator remits to) and is reached by one administrator request with no allow-list, no value validation and no value in the audit record; the administrator role floor limits who can do it but not what it affects, the monthly job that reads the rate is source that runs for every organization with a parent, and no source names the administrator as the owner of the remittance rate or the credit balance, so the route blocks release until the keys the administrator may write are decided and enforced.

defectRegister.title: The platform settings page saves sessionTimeout, mfaEnforcement, passwordMinLength, requireMixedCase, requireSymbol, rateLimitPerMin and webhookUrl into the organization settings JSON through this route, which answers {updated:true}, and the settings page reads them back with defaults (mfaEnforcement admins_only, passwordMinLength 12), but no authentication, session, password, rate-limit or notification code found in the application reads those keys, so an administrator who sets multi-factor enforcement or a password policy is told the setting is saved while nothing enforces it.

PUT /api/settings/organization takes the body without a schema, accepts an empty string or an unbounded string as name, shortName and provinceTerritory, reads the current settings JSON with the shared database handle outside the transaction that writes the merge (so two concurrent saves overwrite each other keys), answers a missing body or organization as a plain error that withApi turns into a 500, and GET answers 200 with organization null for an organization row that does not exist.

handleInboundSms attributes an inbound text message to the organization whose settings JSON holds the called number under twilioPhoneNumber, selecting with limit 1 and no ordering or uniqueness, and the organization settings route lets any organization administrator write that key, so an administrator who stores the number of another organization makes the lookup ambiguous and the inbound message body and sender number can be stored in the conversation table of the wrong organization.

The security events route is configured for readRole and writeRole security_manager with a header comment that describes a privileged reader and a closed forgery path, but security_events is in the DENIED list of the CRUD governance file, so assertCrudRead and assertCrudWrite answer 403 to every caller including a security manager; the privileged reader of the table is the security dashboard page, which checks hasMinRole security_manager and reads the table with SQL under a system context, so the API the comment describes does not exist and the integrity rule for who may author a security event is held only by the governance list.

The storage/usage and storage/cleanup routes are crudRoutes over cms_media_library: GET returns the media library rows of the organization (file name, file url, type, size, folder, tags, uploader) at the member floor, and neither route sums file sizes, reads a quota, compares a file with the references to it or deletes anything, so a caller expecting storage usage receives a page of rows and a caller expecting a cleanup triggers none; the cms_media_library table is read and written by no code other than these two routes and the upload route.

POST /api/storage/usage and POST /api/storage/cleanup insert a cms_media_library row from the whole request body at the steward floor: no file is received or checked, so file_url (any string, including an external address), file_size, mime_type, uploaded_by (any profile user id) and folder are whatever the caller writes, and a library entry can point at a file that does not exist, at an address outside the application storage, or be attributed to another person.

The support/metrics and support/sla routes are crudRoutes over in_app_notifications: GET returns notification rows (user id, title, message, type, action label and url, data, read flag) and POST inserts one, and no route reads or computes a ticket count, response time, resolution time or service-level figure, so a caller expecting support metrics or SLA compliance receives unrelated notification rows; the figures themselves are computed by getTicketMetrics and getSLAMetrics in the support service over support_tickets, and no route calls that service.

GET /api/support/metrics and GET /api/support/sla hold a caller below steward to their own in_app_notifications rows, but any steward or higher role reads the notifications of every user of the organization (title, message, action url and the data object), unbounded by any relationship to the recipient and without a read audit, so notifications that name a member, a case or a grievance are readable beyond the member they were addressed to.

POST /api/support/metrics copies the body into an in_app_notifications row at the steward floor with no check that the user id is a member of the organization (the sibling POST /api/notifications makes that check), with a caller-written title, message and action url and no sender stored, so a steward can store a notification with an arbitrary link for any user id string and it appears to the recipient as a message of the application.

The four support/tickets route files (the collection, tickets/[id], tickets/[id]/assign and tickets/[id]/comments) are crudRoutes over in_app_notifications: GET lists notification rows (user id, title, message, type, action label and url, data, read flag), POST inserts one, and GET, PATCH and DELETE of tickets/[id] read, rewrite and hard delete a notification, while tickets/[id]/assign and tickets/[id]/comments are configured identically to tickets/[id] so the path suffix changes nothing: assigning a ticket or posting a comment is a PATCH of the notification row with that id, and no route creates a ticket, assigns an agent, records a comment or a history entry, although supportTickets, ticketComments and ticketHistory tables and createTicket, assignTicket and addComment in the support service exist and no route calls that service.

The item routes under support/tickets configure writeRole steward and export PATCH and DELETE over in_app_notifications with the factory organization predicate and no owner condition for a caller at the steward floor, so a steward rewrites the title, message, action url, data, read flag and user id of any notification of any user of the organization (the body is applied through the blocked-field filter only) and an administrator permanently removes it, with no relation between the caller and the recipient and no record of the previous value.

POST /api/upload is the generic crudRoutes POST over cms_media_library at the steward write floor: it reads a JSON body into a media library row (file name, file url, size, mime type, folder) and receives and stores no file, while the public job application page posts a multipart form (the file and the folder resumes) to the path and reads the url of the response as the resume address; the route requires a signed-in steward, answers a JSON object whose row is under data (never a url), and GET on the same path lists the media library rows at the member floor, so an applicant sends a file and nothing is stored or addressed.

The four tax route files (tax/slips, tax/t106, tax/rl-1/generate and tax/cope/receipts) are crudRoutes over per_capita_remittances configured at readRole member, and the table has no user, member, e-mail or phone column by the names the low-role guard looks for, so any member of the organization, not only an officer, receives the whole per-capita remittance ledger of the organization (remittance month and year, member counts, per-capita rate, total amount, GL and CLC account codes, approver and rejecter user ids, rejection reason, payment method and reference, remittance and receipt file urls and notes), 50 rows per page by default and 100 at most, whatever tax document the path names, with no field projection and no read audit; the query parameters the COPE receipt viewer sends (memberId, taxYear) are not read.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: Any member of an organization, whatever their role, calls GET /api/tax/slips, /api/tax/t106, /api/tax/rl-1/generate or /api/tax/cope/receipts: readRole is member, the generic factory scopes the rows to the session organization and, because per_capita_remittances has none of the owner or personal column names the low-role guard looks for, applies no owner condition, and it returns whole rows including total_amount, approved_by, rejected_by, rejection_reason, payment_reference and the remittance and receipt file urls.

potentialImpact.description: A member reads the amounts the organization owes and has paid to its parent body, the identity of the officers who approved and rejected each remittance, the reasons for a rejection and the stored remittance and receipt documents, financial records that the remittance run detail route of Gate 0B.6 (DEF-0B6-EMP-REMITTANCE-DETAIL-MEMBER-READ) and the health and welfare path of Gate 0B.8 (DEF-0B8-JUR-HEALTH-WELFARE-PLANS-PATH-IS-THE-PER-CAPITA-REMITTANCE-LEDGER-AT-MEMBER-FLOOR) also place in front of every member.

existingContainment.summary: The factory adds an organization predicate from the session organization, so only the rows of the caller own organization are read; nothing narrows them to an officer, a treasurer or a set of permitted fields, so the exposure is every remittance row of the organization to every member.

releaseDisposition.justification: The routes serve the financial ledger a union owes its parent body to every authenticated member at the lowest role floor with no field projection and no audit; the tenant predicate keeps other organizations out but does not limit a same-organization reader, no source establishes that members are the intended audience of the amounts, the approvers or the stored documents, and the same exposure through the other two per-capita routes was recorded with a lower severity, which this record does not follow because the disclosure is identical and the read blocks release until the institution names the readers.

defectRegister.title: The tax/slips, tax/t106, tax/rl-1/generate and tax/cope/receipts routes are the same crudRoutes configuration over per_capita_remittances and differ only in their path: GET returns remittance rows, and POST is refused with 403 because per_capita_remittances is READ_ONLY in the CRUD governance table, so no route issues, computes or stores a tax slip, a Quebec RL-1, a T106 return or a political contribution receipt although the path names promise each, and the one client that calls a path (the tax dashboard opens the COPE receipt path for a member and a tax year) receives a page of remittance rows in which neither parameter is read.

PATCH and DELETE /api/testimonials/<id> are crudRoutes over the testimonials table with orgScoped false and writeRole admin: the table has no organization column, the role floor is resolved inside the caller own organization, and the update and the hard delete are conditioned on the primary key alone, so an administrator of any organization rewrites (quote, author, role, organization, photo, featured flag, visibility, approval time) or permanently deletes any testimonial the platform shows on its public proof page, and the audit row commits under the organization of that administrator; the storage authority reference already records that any tenant own org-admin can edit or delete this platform-wide content and leaves it for follow-up.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: An administrator of any organization calls PATCH /api/testimonials/<id> with a new quote, author or visibility, or DELETE /api/testimonials/<id>: the factory checks that the caller holds the admin role in the caller own organization, builds the where clause from the primary key alone because orgScoped is false and the table has no organization column, and updates or removes the platform testimonial row in a transaction that audits under the caller organization.

potentialImpact.description: The administrator of one customer organization can replace a named person quote or attribution on the public proof page, mark a testimonial public or featured, or delete the platform testimonials of every other organization, and nothing in the row records which organization or person changed it other than an audit row under the changing administrator own organization.

existingContainment.summary: The caller must hold the administrator role of some organization and the delete is a hard delete with an audit row, so the removal is attributable to an organization; nothing limits the change to platform marketing staff, and the reference record that notes the exposure leaves it for follow-up.

evidence.quote: any tenant's own org-admin can create/edit/delete this platform-wide content

releaseDisposition.justification: The write floor is an administrator title of any customer organization, and the content it changes is shown to every visitor under a named person and organization, so one customer can alter or destroy what the platform attributes to others; the repository already records the exposure and tracks it for follow-up, which establishes that it is known and not that it is contained, and no source names a platform marketing office that should hold the write.

defectRegister.title: GET /api/testimonials/<id> selects the row by primary key at the member read floor and returns every column, whatever the row visibility (the column defaults to public and holds other values) and whatever its approval time (null until approved), so any signed-in member of any organization reads a testimonial that has not been approved or is not public, with its quote, author, role, organization and photo; the public proof page does not read this route and describes its content as anonymized composites.

The testimonial approval component sends PATCH /api/testimonials/<id> with status, reviewedAt and reviewedBy (approved or rejected) and reports success, and the testimonials table has no status, reviewedAt or reviewedBy column and carries approvedAt, which the component never sends, so an approval or a rejection records no decision in any column the table has and the route answers success for it.

GET /api/units and GET /api/units/<id> are crudRoutes over bargaining_units at the member read floor and the table has none of the user, member, e-mail or phone column names the low-role guard looks for, so any member of the organization receives every register row with its certification number, body and dates, contract expiry and next bargaining date, chief steward and bargaining chair user ids, classifications, free-text notes and custom fields object, with no field projection and no read audit.

POST /api/units and PATCH /api/units/<id> are configured at writeRole steward with the whole body copied into the row, so any steward of the organization creates a bargaining unit or rewrites its certification number, certification body and dates, current collective agreement id, contract and bargaining dates, member count, chief steward and bargaining chair, and an administrator archives it, with no check that the caller represents the unit and with the audit row listing field names and no values.

GET /api/worksites and GET /api/worksites/<id> are crudRoutes over worksites at the member read floor, so any member of the organization receives every worksite row with the site manager name, e-mail address and telephone number, the address and coordinates, the employee and shift counts, free-text notes and the custom fields object, with no field projection and no read audit, and the worksite management screen and the unit and committee screens load the whole list from the route.

POST and PATCH on the unit and worksite routes copy the body into the row, and employer_id, worksite_id, chief_steward_id and bargaining_chair_id are foreign keys to the employers, worksites and profiles tables that carry no organization condition, so the row can name an employer, a worksite or a person of another organization (the foreign key check passes for any existing id) and the register then joins organizations that have nothing to do with each other.

The wcb/claims and wcb/claims/[id] routes are crudRoutes over wcb_claims configured at the steward floor for reads and writes (the collection declares an owner column workerId, the item route none), and wcb_claims is DENIED in the CRUD governance table, so assertCrudRead and assertCrudWrite refuse every call with 403 before a query or an audit row, for stewards and administrators alike; the route header describes a claim collection a steward lists and creates, the claim holds the medical and prognosis detail of an injured worker, and if the governance entry is ever lifted every steward of the organization would read and rewrite every claim (the item route has no owner condition), with no relation to the representative who holds the member case.

GET /api/wcb/assessments and GET /api/wcb/assessments/<id> are crudRoutes over wcb_employer_assessments at the steward read floor, so any steward of the organization (not only the officers who record the assessments) receives every assessment row with the premium rate, assessable payroll, premium due, experience rating, surcharge or refund, due and paid dates, status, document ids and the metadata object, with no field projection and no read audit.

GET /api/targets/summary is configured at the member floor and returns every kpi_configurations row of the organization with the whole row spread into the response (`...cfg`): the calculation record (formula, aggregation and filters), the alert recipients (user ids or e-mail addresses), the id of the creator and the dashboard layout reach any member of the organization, not the officers who create targets, with no field projection and no read audit.

The summary takes the current value of a target from the latest analytics_metrics row of the organization whose metric_type text equals the target metric type (one query per target through the shared database handle) and applies neither the data source (claims, members, financial, custom_query) nor the calculation the target declares, so a target is judged against whatever row carries the same type name, and a row of another unit or period that shares the text is read as the current value; the progress figure divides that value by the target value.

computeHealth returns critical when the current value is at or below the critical threshold, at risk when it is at or below the warning threshold and on track otherwise, for every target: a target whose good direction is downward (resolution time, backlog, grievance count) is reported critical when its figure is low and on track when its figure is high, and the route stores no direction.

POST /api/targets stores a free-form calculation record (any key and value, defaulted to a sum), an alertEnabled flag and a data source, and the summary route reads none of the calculation or the data source and no code found reads alertEnabled to send an alert: the insert writes no alertRecipients value at all, so a target created with alertEnabled true promises an alert that no recipient list and no sender exists to deliver.

PATCH /api/targets/<id> compares the path id with the uuid column kpi_configurations.id without a shape check, so a malformed id raises a database error that the wrapper answers as a 500 instead of a 404, and the route offers no way to edit, rename or delete a target: the only change available after creation is the active flag.

GET /api/users/me/organizations, in its legacy branch (entered whenever UE_CANONICAL_BOOTSTRAP_V2 is not 1), links membership rows to the caller when the caller has none: it takes the e-mail address from the identity provider user (or the profile row), selects every organization_members row of any organization whose lower-cased e-mail equals it and runs an update that sets user_id to the caller on all of them, with no condition on the current user_id (a row already bound to another person is rewritten), no verified-address check, no role limit, no organization limit and no audit record; if no row carries the e-mail, a second statement sets user_id to the caller on every membership of the legacy user id of any profile that shares the e-mail; the response then lists the organizations and the roles that were taken, and the whole sequence runs inside a GET with the shared database handle.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: A signed-in person who has no membership row bound to their user id and whose identity-provider e-mail address equals (ignoring case) the e-mail of membership rows of one or several organizations calls GET /api/users/me/organizations while UE_CANONICAL_BOOTSTRAP_V2 is not 1: the route rewrites user_id on every such row, including rows already bound to another user id, and returns those organizations and the roles of the rewritten rows; the legacy profile fallback rewrites every membership of another user id when a profile with the same e-mail exists.

potentialImpact.description: A person whose address matches, or an attacker who registers the same address with the identity provider, takes over the memberships (and the roles, including administrator) that another person holds in every organization where the address appears, displacing the legitimate holder from those organizations, and receives each organization record, with no audit record of the re-binding.

existingContainment.summary: The re-binding runs only in the legacy branch and only when the caller has no membership bound to their own user id; the canonical branch (UE_CANONICAL_BOOTSTRAP_V2 equal to 1) returns before any e-mail lookup. currentStateContextEnabled is true only when the variable equals 1, so an unset variable keeps the legacy branch reachable, and no source in the application proves the variable is 1 in every deployment.

releaseDisposition.justification: The statement that moves the memberships has no condition tying the row to the caller (no unlinked-row predicate, no verified e-mail, no audit), it can rewrite rows of several organizations at once, and the exposure is reached by any signed-in person with the right address, so the legacy branch blocks release until the canonical branch is the only branch or the linking authority is decided and enforced.

defectRegister.title: In the legacy branch a user id listed in PLATFORM_ADMIN_USER_IDS receives up to 500 organization records (name, slug, type, parent, sector, jurisdiction, description) whatever their memberships, and every other caller causes the route to select the whole organizations table and filter it in memory by the ids and slugs of the caller memberships, so the cost grows with every organization of the platform and the platform list is held by an environment list the application cannot audit.

The legacy branch logs the full e-mail address of the caller (email: userEmail) when it links memberships by e-mail and a three-letter preview of it in another line, together with the user id, so a log reader receives the address that the re-binding was made on.

The response replaces a missing createdAt or updatedAt of an organization, and a missing joinedAt and createdAt of a membership, with the time of the call (new Date().toISOString()), so a record without a stored time is returned with a time that never existed.

The /api/v2/[...path] catch-all is exported as GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE by one handler that answers HTTP 200 with a deprecation object for every method and path: the dues report page posts /api/v2/admin/reports/generate and treats a response that is ok as a generated report, the user role selector puts a role change to /api/v2/admin/users/role and shows the toast Role updated on an ok response, and the staff page posts remittance approve and reject to /api/v2/clc/remittances/<id>/approve and /reject and logs Approved remittance on an ok response, while the file that builds a 410 Gone response (goneResponse) exists and the catch-all never calls it, so a write to a removed path is reported to its caller as a success and nothing is written.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: Any signed-in member (the catch-all requires the member floor) who triggers a client that still writes to a /api/v2 path receives HTTP 200 for the POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE: the dues report page treats the answer as a generated report, the export button downloads the deprecation JSON as a file named as a report, the role selector confirms a role change that was not made and the remittance approve and reject actions record an approval that was not made.

potentialImpact.description: An administrator is told that a role was changed, a report was generated or a remittance was approved or rejected when no write happened; the person believes a role was granted or removed and a payment decision was made, and the application logs the approval, so the institution acts on an outcome that did not occur.

activationEvidence.quote: if (!res.ok) throw new Error('Failed to update role');

existingContainment.summary: The response carries a deprecated flag in the body and Deprecation and Sunset headers, which a caller that tests only the response status does not read; the server action of the staff page sends no session cookie in the call, so it may be refused by the member floor before it reaches the 200, and no component that imports the role selector was found.

releaseDisposition.justification: The repository rule is that a capability that is not implemented answers 501 (or 410 for a removed path) and never HTTP 200; the catch-all answers 200 to every write at the member floor and several callers read the 200 as a completed administrative action, so the route blocks release until it answers a refusal for every method.

defectRegister.title: GET on a removed /api/v2 path answers HTTP 200 with an object whose keys are _deprecated, _message, _sunset and _canonical, where the callers (the push device manager, the social media post composer, the benchmark and scheduled report consoles, the federation remittances and compliance pages) read the body as the list or figures they requested, so a console renders an empty state or no data with no signal that its endpoint was removed.

The catch-all calls logDeprecatedAccess(v2Path, request.method, canonical) with no user id and no organization id and does not await it, and logDeprecatedAccess swallows a failure of the audit write, so the api.deprecated_access event names a path and a method and no actor, and its loss is silent.

The deprecation module holds the sunset date as a constant (2026-07-07) that it prints in the body and the Sunset header, and nothing compares it with the current time or changes the answer after it, so the route keeps answering 200 with a sunset that has passed and no removal is scheduled in source.

GET /api/tenant/current answers HTTP 200 with an org whose name, slug and subscriptionTier are constant null and whose features list is empty, and an availableOrgs list that holds only that same org, so a legacy client that reads the organization name or tier receives a success with no data; the route reads no organization row, and no caller in the application calls it.

GET /api/test-auth is a plain route (no wrapper, no role floor, no production guard) that any signed-in user can call: it sends the session token as a bearer to the Django address held in the NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL build variable (localhost:8000 when unset), returns the status and body of the backend health and /me/ answers, the session user id and organization, whether a token exists and the text of any fetch error (String(e)), so the response discloses backend addresses and error details and the diagnostic ships in every build.

GET /api/union-eyes/queue-status accepts either the service key header or any signed-in session (requireApiAuth with no role, no organization requirement), and returns the pending, active, failed and retry counts of the whole background queue, the per-queue counts and the task id, task name, status and completion time of the 20 most recent failed tasks, which are platform-wide operational data not scoped to an organization, to a signed-in member.

The queue status route sends every error, including the refusal that requireApiAuth throws for a caller with no session, through one catch that answers HTTP 503 with availability error and detail String(err), so an unauthenticated call is reported as an outage and the text of the underlying error (a connection string error of the queue backend, for example) is returned to the caller; when no Django address is configured the route answers 200 with availability not_configured and a null queue.

The service credential of the route is the AI_SERVICE_KEY environment value, the same key that the AI service uses, compared with the request header by a plain equality (===) and not a constant-time comparison, and the control plane sends it on every telemetry call, so one key opens the queue figures and the AI service and cannot be rotated for one without the other.

POST /api/triage-designations passes caseAssigneeEligible (the case policy role that may add an internal note, or ue_case_assignee_authorized in the canonical branch) as the eligibility test for a designation of either scope, while the message queue decides use of a messages designation with the conversation assignee roles (membershipStillEligible), so a messages designation can be refused to a person who is an eligible conversation assignee and granted to a person who is a case assignee and not a conversation assignee, whose designation then grants nothing.

grantDesignation closes a lapsed live designation by setting revokedAt to now and revokedBy to the string system:expiry before the new grant, in the same transaction, and writes no audit row for the closure (only the grant is audited), so the end of an expired designation is a data change with no audit record and a revoker value that is not a user.

DELETE /api/triage-designations takes the designation id from a JSON request body (body: revokeSchema), a pattern that HTTP intermediaries and many clients drop or ignore for DELETE, and the route has no path id; no caller in the application sends the request.

The vocabulary routes serve, as reference data of the grievance system, hard-coded service-level hours (24 hours for critical, 48 high, 72 medium, 168 low), severity legal-review flags, per-role canAssign, canEscalate and canSettle flags for roles named member, steward, chief_steward, business_agent, officer and admin, and a status machine with the roles allowed to make each transition, from a package whose header calls them defaults, with no cited source, no approval and no relation to the roles the application enforces; the flags are not read by any enforcing code found, and a client that treats them as the institution service levels or permissions would present an unsourced figure as institutional.

Every vocabulary route sets Cache-Control public with max-age 3600 on a response that is behind a signed-in session, so a shared cache or proxy may store and serve the response to callers without a session for an hour.

getCUPEVocabulary sets lastUpdated to the time of the call and version to the constant 0.1.0, so the full vocabulary route reports a last update of now on every request and a version that does not change when the content changes.

POST /api/voice/transcribe, at the steward floor, applies no rate limit and no entitlement check and writes no audit record, while the sibling upload route applies a rate limit and an entitlement check: a steward (or a script holding a steward session) can send repeated 25 MB recordings, each up to the 60-second function limit, to the speech service with no count and no record of who transcribed what.

The transcribe response sets duration to audioFile.size (the size of the upload in bytes, with the comment Approximate), so a caller that reads duration receives a number of bytes presented as a length of time.

Both voice routes read the uploaded recording into memory and send it to an external Azure service (the speech service in the transcribe route, an Azure OpenAI Whisper deployment in the upload route), and the recordings are spoken claim descriptions that can name a person, an employer and a medical or disciplinary matter: neither route records a consent, names a processor agreement or region, records the disclosure or states a retention, and the upload route logs the body of a failed processor answer.

POST /api/voice/upload checks the ai_search entitlement of the organization (and labels a refusal voice_upload) for a transcription feature, and checkEntitlement only reads settings.credits and consumes none, so the check neither meters the transcription nor reflects a voice entitlement; no caller of the route exists in the application.

POST /api/workspace/telemetry accepts the allow-listed event name and logs every allow-listed payload key, of which tab and timestamp are written as the client string with no length bound or format check (route is checked against the static route list), with no rate limit, so a member can write arbitrarily long strings of their choice into the application log at any rate, and the figures the route exists to produce live only in log lines.

For a workbook with no claimed_by_user_id, resolveClaimedWorkbookAuthority returns the preclaim authority from the workbook identifier alone, so GET, POST, PATCH and DELETE on /api/workbook/<id>/memory-holders run in the system context for any caller who presents that identifier, with no session, with no guardPublicIntake or other rate limit (the route files import none), and auditClaimedWorkbookWrite returns at once for a preclaim authority so the create, update and delete are not recorded; the same identifier is returned by the public start route and placed in the checkout redirect addresses, and each write may carry a display name and notes of up to 4,000 characters.

After the claim, a same-organization peer is any signed-in person for whom getOrganizationIdForUser returns the claimed organization (that function selects an organization by a client cookie after a membership check): resolveClaimedWorkbookAuthority applies no role floor, and the memory-holder routes then let that person list, create, change and delete holders in the system context, with a display name and notes naming individuals who have no notice that they are recorded, and the PATCH and DELETE audit rows are written only when a row changed.

POST /api/workbook/start accepts consent as an optional object (consentToPersist and a time), inserts the workbook whether or not the object is present or true (consent is stored as null when absent) and logs only the workbook id and locale; no route of the workbook product reads workbooks.consent before it stores a memory holder, creates a checkout session or exports, so the consent the visitor gave or withheld changes nothing the product does.

guardPublicIntake keys its per-client limit (20 starts per hour, 10 checkouts per hour) on the first of cf-connecting-ip, x-real-ip or the first x-forwarded-for entry, all request headers a client can set when the application is not behind a proxy that overwrites them, and neither public route reads a challenge token, so a caller can create workbooks and open Stripe checkout sessions at a rate the limit does not bound.

POST /api/workbook/checkout reads the workbook through the shared database handle (import { db } from '@/db') outside withSystemContext, withRLSContext and withClaimedWorkbookAccess, so the handle is the pooled runtime connection with no app.current_user_id; the closure migration creates the user isolation policy on workbooks over claimed_by_user_id, whose select policy compares that column with app.current_user_id, so an unclaimed workbook (the only kind a buyer has before paying) is not visible to the read and the route would answer 404 for it; the start and claim routes use withSystemContext for the same table, and the runtime proof of the policy is outstanding.

POST /api/workbook/checkout sends the workbook identifier, which is the bearer credential for the memory holders of an unclaimed workbook, to Stripe in metadata.workbook_id and in the success and cancel addresses (/workbook/<id>?tier_unlocked=workbook_self_guided), so the credential is held by the payment processor, appears in the browser history and referrer chain of the buyer and is logged with the session id, and no source states the processor agreement or the lifecycle of the identifier.

When NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL is not set the checkout success and cancel addresses fall back to http://localhost:3000, and the route tests only that the workbook is not already at the self-guided tier, so each call creates a new Stripe session with no pending-session or idempotency check and a buyer or script can open any number of sessions for one workbook.

POST /api/workbook/<id>/claim requires a session but applies no rate limit and reads the body with request.json() without a size cap, and a request whose id and token match a row but whose claim has lapsed is answered 409 or 410 while a miss is answered 404, so a signed-in caller can try claim tokens against an identifier at the speed of the application.

GET /api/workbook/<id>/export builds a PDF of the carrier register (role, criticality, tenure, successor and the free-text responsibility of every memory holder, with the cartography) for a claimant or any same-organization peer and writes no audit record of the read; loadWorkbookModules also selects the display name of every holder into memory although the template does not print it.

The start, checkout and claim routes write the workbook identifier, which is the bearer credential of an unclaimed workbook, to the application log (with the locale, the Stripe session id, or the user id and organization id), so anyone who reads the log can use the identifier on the memory-holder routes until the workbook is claimed.
